item.content:encoded:
MLB.com: Yesterday afternoon, Major League Baseball announced the finalists for this year's Hank Aaron Award. Recognizing the two best offensive performances (one in each league), the award is conferred through a fan vote and a panel consisting of journalists and former players. Yankees first baseman/designated hitter Ben Rice finds himself as one of this year's finalists, hoping to make it the three straight season (and fourth in five years) that a Yankees slugger takes home the award (Aaron Judge won it in 2022, 2024, and 2025). Other nominees include Baltimore's Pete Alonso, Houston's Yordan Alvarez (the likely favorite), and Kansas City's Bobby Witt Jr.
The Athletic | Clark Gilmore: Clarke Gilmore, a current member of the Savannah Bananas and a former teammate of Ben Rice at Dartmouth, penned a guest article for The Athletic's Peak newsletter, a series focusing on the mental side of sports. As you might have guessed based on the nature of the series, Gilmore spoke not about Rice's physical prowess, but on his "consistency" that dated back to his college days — and could be seen not only on the diamond, but in much more mundane things, such as Mario Kart in the dorms.
FanGraphs | Matt Martell: Turning our attention from one Massachusetts boy to another, Cam Schlittler came out with a completely unexpected strategy against the Red Sox in Game 1 of the ALWC: the typically fastball-dominant youngster threw 32 curveballs — a whopping 27.4 percent of the time (during the regular season, he threw it just 9.8 percent of the time). The start was the culmination of a year-long process in which the Cy Young favorite working to turn his curveball into a veritable weapon, one that can can make him a dangerous pitcher not just now, but going forward.

item.content:encoded:
2 trades Astros must make this offseason after early postseason exit appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Houston Astros cannot react to an early postseason exit with minor roster adjustments. After finishing 81-81 and getting swept by the Chicago White Sox in the American League Wild Card Series, Houston needs to attack its two weaknesses: its rotation and an offense lacking speed and dependable outfield production.
This is still a roster built to compete around Yordan Alvarez, Jose Altuve, Carlos Correa, Jeremy Peña and Hunter Brown. However, the Astros need more than a depth starter and a platoon outfielder if they intend to make another serious run in 2027.
Houston should pursue two aggressive trades. Neither would be inexpensive, but both would address a major weakness without forcing the organization into a rebuild.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Trade for Mariners ace Logan Gilbert
Astros receive: RHP Logan Gilbert
Mariners receive: INF Xavier Neyens, RHP Ethan Pecko and OF Joseph Sullivan
Trading within the AL West would create an obvious obstacle, but Houston should still call Seattle about Gilbert. The 29-year-old is entering his final year before free agency, making him a logical trade candidate if the Mariners do not believe they can sign him to an extension.
Gilbert would give the Astros the durable frontline starter they lacked throughout 2026. He finished the season with a 12-11 record, 3.73 ERA, 1.09 WHIP and 205 strikeouts across 186 innings. His career numbers are equally strong: a 3.60 ERA, 1.06 WHIP and 1,089 strikeouts over 1,021 1/3 innings.
Pairing Gilbert with Brown would give Houston two legitimate postseason starters and reduce pressure on a rotation ravaged by injuries. The Astros used a franchise-record 18 starters in 2026, and Brown lasted only two-thirds of an inning while allowing four runs in the decisive Wild Card loss.
Seattle would demand a premium for trading an established starter to a division rival. Neyens, Houston's No. 2 prospect, offers significant left-handed power, while Pecko supplies a near-major-league arm and Sullivan adds outfield depth.
That price would hurt a thin farm system, especially with Neyens ranked among MLB's Top 100 prospects. Still, prospects are assets, and Gilbert would address the Astros' most important weakness immediately. Houston should make the trade only with confidence that it can extend him beyond 2027.
Buy low on Jarren Duran
Astros receive: OF Jarren Duran
Red Sox receive: OF Logan Hughes and RHP Bryce Mayer
Duran's value dropped sharply during a disappointing 2026 season, creating a potential buy-low opportunity. He hit .207 with a .266 on-base percentage and .361 slugging percentage, although he still produced 20 home runs and 21 stolen bases in 151 games.
Those numbers are a significant step backward from his 2024 breakout, when he batted .285 with an .834 OPS, 21 homers and 34 steals. His combination of speed, extra-base ability and experience in left and center field would give Houston an element missing from its current lineup.
The risk is obvious. Duran struck out 165 times in 2026 and posted a .627 OPS, so Houston would be betting that a change of scenery and different hitting instruction could revive him. However, he remains under club control for two more seasons, giving the Astros time to recover value.
Boston would receive Houston's No. 3 prospect in Hughes and a pitching prospect in Mayer. Houston would keep its top prospect, Kevin Alvarez, while acquiring an athletic outfielder who could lead off, create pressure on the bases and move around defensively.
Neither trade guarantees another championship, but standing still is the greater danger. Gilbert would stabilize October pitching, while Duran would make the lineup faster and less dependent on home runs. Those are precisely the bold changes Houston needs after another brief postseason appearance.

item.content:encoded:
The National League Division Series between the Atlanta Braves and Los Angeles Dodgers is tied 1-1.
The Dodgers won the first game of the series 5-3 on Saturday. The Braves won the second game 3-2 on Sunday.
Game 3 of the Braves-Dodgers series is scheduled to begin at 6:00 p.m. EDT on Tuesday at Truist Park.
Ahead of Game 3, the Braves made a major Matt Olson announcement.
Atlanta Braves Announce Matt Olson News Before NLDS Game 3 vs. Dodgers
ATLANTA, GEORGIA – OCTOBER 01: Matt Olson #28 of the Atlanta Braves celebrates a home run against the Philadelphia Phillies during the seventh inning in game three of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park on October 01, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Edward M. Pio Roda/Getty Images)
The Braves announced that Matt Olson has been nominated for the 2026 Hank Aaron Award.
Congratulations to Matt Olson for being our 2026 Hank Aaron Award Finalist!
Vote for Matt: mlb.com/hank-aaron-awa
From MLB.com: The Hank Aaron Award is awarded annually to the best overall offensive performer in each league. The award was introduced in 1999 to mark the 25th anniversary of Hank Aaron breaking Babe Ruth’s all-time home run record. A panel of Hall of Famers combines with a fan vote to determine the winners.
Here are the other NL nominees:
- Washington Nationals INF CJ Abrams
- Milwaukee Brewers 1B Jake Bauers
- Chicago Cubs CF Pete Crow-Armstrong
- Cincinnati Reds SS Elly De La Cruz
- Los Angeles Dodgers DH Shohei Ohtani
- Philadelphia Phillies DH Kyle Schwarber
- Cincinnati Reds 1B Sal Stewart
- San Diego Padres RF Fernando Tatis Jr.
- St. Louis Cardinals OF Jordan Walker
CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – SEPTEMBER 24: Pete Crow-Armstrong #4 of the Chicago Cubs steals second base during the first inning against the Miami Marlins at Wrigley Field on September 24, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jayden Mack/Getty Images)
Here are the AL nominees:
- Baltimore Orioles 1B Pete Alonso
- Houston Astros DH Yordan Alvarez
- Seattle Mariners LF Randy Arozarena
- Tampa Bay Rays 3B Junior Caminero
- Boston Red Sox 1B Willson Contreras
- Tampa Bay Rays 1B Yandy Díaz
- Detroit Tigers LF Riley Greene
- New York Yankees DH/1B Ben Rice
- Chicago White Sox 3B Miguel Vargas
- Kansas City Royals SS Bobby Witt Jr.
Looking at Matt Olson
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 04: Matt Olson #28 of the Atlanta Braves looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Dodgers in game two of the National League Division Series at Dodger Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ryan Sirius Sun/Getty Images)
Olson posted 4.4 bWAR and a .251/.321/.502 slash line with 41 home runs and 93 RBI over 162 games in the 2026 regular season.
He has gone 3-for-19 with a home run and two walks in the 2026 playoffs so far.
Olson has 11 years of big-league experience. He spent the first six years of his career with the Oakland Athletics before joining the Braves.
Throughout his career, Olson has posted 44.2 bWAR and a .256/.347/.507 batting line with 329 home runs and 901 RBI. He is a four-time All-Star, three-time Gold Glove Award Winner and a one-time Silver Slugger Award winner.

item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong will add a lot of hardware over the next few weeks.
Crow-Armstrong is the favorite to win the National League MVP over Shohei Ohtani. He will definitely win his second straight Gold Glove and could even take home his first platinum glove after a phenomenal defensive season.
Well, there's another award that Crow-Armstrong could win.
The Cubs outfielder is listed as a finalist for the Hank Aaron Award. This award has been given out annually since 1999 and is given to the most outstanding offensive player in both the National League and the American League.
Crow-Armstrong is one of 10 finalists for this award in the National League. He is joined by CJ Abrams (Washington Nationals), Jake Bauers (Milwaukee Brewers), Elly De La Cruz (Cincinnati Reds), Shohei Ohtani (Los Angeles Dodgers), Matt Olson (Atlanta Braves), Kyle Schwarber (Philadelphia Phillies), Sal Stewart (Cincinnati Reds), Fernando Tatis Jr. (San Diego Padres), and Jordan Walker (St. Louis Cardinals).
A panel of Hall of Famers, combined with a fan vote, determines the winner of this award. Fans can vote for Crow-Armstrong right now. Voting will be open for one week and will close on Monday, October 12, at 11:59 AM ET.
Crow-Armstrong should be the favorite to win this prestigious award. He was the best offensive player in baseball by WAR this season. His 8.3 offensive WAR on ESPN was the highest in baseball, ahead of hitters like Yordan Alvarez (7.2) and De La Cruz (6.4).
There's a reason why Crow-Armstrong led the league in offensive WAR in the regular season. The 24-year-old slashed .280/.372/.570 with 45 home runs, 31 doubles, eight triples, 107 RBI, and 41 stolen bases across 162 games.
Crow-Armstrong's 45 home runs were tied for the league lead, and his .570 slugging percentage and .942 OPS were the best marks in the National League. He also led the league in runs scored (119) and ranked fourth in the majors in RBI (107).
It would be quite surprising if Crow-Armstrong doesn't win the Hank Aaron Award in the National League. He ranked in the top half of the league in several offensive categories and showed up in big moments all through the season.
Crow-Armstrong is looking to become the fourth Cubs player to win this award. Sammy Sosa won the first award in 1999, Aramis Ramirez then won it in 2008, and Kris Bryant won it during his MVP season in 2016. The Cubs young outfielder could be next.

item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Tigers made one of their best draft choices in the 2019 MLB Draft, taking outfielder Riley Greene with the fifth overall pick. Since Greene debuted for the Tigers, he's become known as the face of the offense, collecting multiple achievements along the way.
A three-time All-Star from 2024 to 2026, a Silver Slugger Award winner in 2025, and a reliable defender, Greene leads the Detroit offense into the future. It was proof enough when Greene went down with an injury in August that this offense needs him, but that's a good thing to have within the organization.
With the offseason in full swing for the Tigers, nominations for the prestigious Hank Aaron Award have been released as the playoffs continue.
The Hank Aaron Award is awarded annually to the best overall offensive performer in each league. The award was introduced in 1999 to mark the 25th anniversary of Hank Aaron breaking Babe Ruth's all-time home run record. A panel of Hall of Famers combines with a fan vote to determine the winners.
Of the 10 American League players representing 10 American League teams, Greene takes center stage for the Tigers organization.
How to Vote for Riley Greene
Greene finished his 2026 campaign with 21 home runs, 75 RBIs and an OPS of .844. While his home run and RBI totals were down from his 2025 campaign, the All-Star outfielder set a new career-high in OPS and doubles with 32.
Voting is open through Oct. 12, and Greene needs all the votes he can get from Tigers fans. Some of his biggest competitors for the award this season are Yordan Alvarez of the Houston Astros, Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays, and Ben Rice of the New York Yankees.
Of all the American League nominees, Greene ranked ninth in home runs, ninth in RBIs, and seventh in OPS. If Greene brings home the hardware, he will become the first Tigers player to do so since Miguel Cabrera won the award in back-to-back MVP seasons in 2012 and 2013.
If Greene doesn't win, it doesn't take away from how much improvement he had in 2026. A big flaw in Greene's game was strikeouts, punching out the most in Major League Baseball in 2025 with 201. He lowered that total to 157 in 2026 and improved his overall offense.
Greene is easily the top candidate to get a contract extension to ensure Detroit has a well-rounded athlete on their roster for years to come.
Dominic Minchella is a 2024 Eastern Michigan University graduate with a BA in Communications, Media, and Theatre Arts and a Journalism minor. He covers Major League Baseball for On SI and spends his free time watching games and sharing his insights.

item.content:encoded:
The season for the Houston Astros came to an unceremonious close at the hands of the Chicago White Sox, who beat them two games to none in the MLB Wild Card Playoff round.
Now, the White Sox move on to face the divisional rival Cleveland Guardians in the Divisional Playoff round, while the Astros are left picking up the pieces and wondering where things went wrong.
Not long afterward, starter Hunter Brown expressed his frustration with how things turned out in a completely blunt recap.
Houston Astros Pitcher Hunter Brown Admits The Tough Truth After Series Loss To White Sox
Brown's start in Game 2 against the White Sox ended before the first inning was over, forcing the Astros to turn to their bullpen early. The Astros had already utilized eight pitchers during their Game 1 setback, and they also used six more in their regular season finale.
Brown faced nine Chicago batters, allowing five hits and four runs, three of which were earned. He also walked one batter and while also not getting much help from his teammates. The Astros committed a pair of costly errors, while Yordan Alvarez failed to catch a playable fly ball.
Ultimately, the White Sox picked up a 7-3 win, sweeping the Astros out of the playoffs and ending their dreams of another World Series run.
Afterward, Brown said that his performance wasn't up to snuff despite his best efforts.
"I feel like everything that could have went poorly did and I didn't overcome the whole inning, really," Brown said, per Brian McTaggart of MLB.com. "I felt like, looking back, it's hard to say I don't take anything back, but I feel like pitches that I threw I was confident and I threw them to the best of my ability. Just didn't come out on the right end of it. Unfortunately, that's the way it went, and they were able to slap a crooked number up there on the board."
A shoulder strain limited Brown's availability during the 2026 regular season, which saw him finish with a 3.19 ERA in 20 starts.
Hunter Brown Has Played His Entire MLB Career With The Astros
Brown was taken by the Astros in the fifth round (166th overall pick) of the 2019 MLB Draft. After making his professional debut that year, he missed the entire 2020 minor league season before moving through Double-A and Triple-A in 2021.
Brown broke out in 2022 with Triple-A Sugar Land, posting a 2.55 ERA and 106 innings while earning PCL Pitcher of the Year honors. His performance also made him Houston's top prospect and one of MLB's most highly regarded young pitchers.
Brown helped Houston win the 2022 World Series before becoming a full-time starter in 2023. After a strong second half in 2024, he broke out in 2025 with a 2.43 ERA, 206 strikeouts and his first All-Star selection.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

item.content:encoded:
Published Oct 2, 2026 10:17 am
NEW YORK (AP) — Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the Baseball Digest major league player of the year award Friday, and Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski was selected pitcher of the year.
San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller was chosen reliever of the year.
Crow-Armstrong batted .280 with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases this season, becoming the seventh member of the 40-40 club.
He led the majors in runs (119), tied for most homers, ranked second in OPS (.943) and finished fourth in RBIs (107). All while playing outstanding defense and appearing in all 162 regular-season games to help the Cubs earn a National League wild card.
The 24-year-old Crow-Armstrong received 21 of 24 first-place votes in balloting by a panel of baseball writers, broadcasters, reporters and researchers that included several former players, managers and executives.
Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez finished second.
Crow-Armstrong became the seventh Cubs player to win the Baseball Digest award and first since Kris Bryant and Anthony Rizzo shared the prize in 2016.
The hard-throwing Misiorowski also garnered 21 first-place votes after going 16-5 to propel Milwaukee to the best record in the big leagues (103-59) and its fourth consecutive NL Central title. He led the majors with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts in 30 starts covering 174 2/3 innings.
New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler was runner-up to the 24-year-old Misiorowski, the first Brewers pitcher to take home the honor.
Miller, 28, tied for the NL lead with a career-high 38 saves as the Padres earned a wild-card spot in the playoffs. He went 5-2 with a 1.67 ERA and 129 strikeouts in 70 innings over 66 appearances.
The right-hander received 18 first-place votes and easily outpaced Cleveland Guardians closer Cade Smith, who came in second.

item.content:encoded:
By KRISTIE RIEKEN AP Sports Writer
HOUSTON (AP) — From 100 losses to their first playoff series win in two decades, these scrappy Chicago White Sox just keep outdoing themselves.
The White Sox used a big first inning and a three-run homer from Chase Meidroth to propel them to a 7-3 win over the Houston Astros on Wednesday to sweep their AL Wild Card Series.
“I’m proud of the guys and certainly happy for them as they’re probably the only ones in this country that believed that they could be in this spot,” manager Will Venable said. “And they maintained that belief in the beginning of the season and went throughout the season maintaining that, and they made it happen. So it’s awesome to get to this point.”
It’s the first time Chicago has won a playoff series since beating Houston in the World Series in 2005. Under the direction of Venable, the second-year skipper, and with a letter of support from Pope Leo XIV, the White Sox advanced to face AL Central champion Cleveland in the AL Division Series beginning Saturday in Cleveland.
“It means everything for our fans,” Meidroth said. “They have been incredible all year. So the main thing was getting back to Chicago for some postseason baseball, and so we’re really blessed that we get to do that.”
The White Sox, who lost 100 games in each of the last three seasons, are the only team in major league history to follow consecutive 100-loss seasons with a playoff berth.
The AL West-winning Astros went 81-81 to become the first team to reach the postseason without a winning record. Their recent playoff woes in Houston continued Wednesday as they dropped their ninth straight home playoff game in a ninth trip to the postseason in the last 10 years.
Chicago pounced on the Astros for four runs in the first inning a day after scoring three in the first two innings of a 6-3 win. Houston ace Hunter Brown was lifted after getting just two outs and wasn’t helped by a sloppy defense which committed two first-inning errors.
He was 6-0 with a 2.39 ERA in six career starts against the White Sox before Wednesday’s debacle.
The Astros clawed their way back into it with solo home runs from Jeremy Peña, Cam Smith and Jose Altuve to trail by 1 entering the sixth inning.
AJ Blubaugh, who opened Game 1, and Peter Lambert, pitching on two days’ rest, combined to retire the next 13 batters after Brown exited. Chicago’s next baserunner came when Lambert walked Andrew Benintendi to start the sixth and then walked Tristan Peters.
Bryan Abreu came in, and Meidroth smashed his fifth pitch off the wall in left field to push the lead to 7-3. He yelled on his entire trip around the bases to the delight of a patch of White Sox fans seated near the visitor’s dugout.
“I was looking for something middle up,” Meidroth said. “He’s had my number all year, really good fastball, so I got something middle up and I was able to cash in for the team. So, yeah, that was awesome.”
Houston faced boos for a second game in a row from an unusually thin crowd. It’s a second straight playoff trip where the Astros have been swept at home in the wild card after losing both games to Detroit in 2024.
Now they’ll face an uncertain future with manager Joe Espada’s contract set to expire at season’s end after general manager Dana Brown was fired last month.
“We fought back and we set our goal to win this division and we accomplished that,” Espada said. “We wanted to play deep in October. We came short on that. But just the way our guys stayed together and were able to get this far, extremely proud of our team.”
It was a disappointing series for Houston slugger and AL MVP-favorite Yordan Alvarez, who managed only a single with two strikeouts in eight at-bats in the series.
Altuve’s shot to the seats in left field in the fourth inning got the Astros within 4-3. It was the 28th postseason homer of his career, which is second in MLB history behind Manny Ramirez (29).
“We’re all sad,” Altuve said. “We wanted to go to the World Series and win it. But today is sorrow for the final day of the season.”
The Astros had a shot to take the lead before Meidroth’s homer. They loaded the bases with two outs in the fifth, but Anthony Kay retired Altuve on a fly out to end the inning.
___

item.content:encoded:
La segunda jornada de la Serie de Comodín en la temporada de las Grandes Ligas (MLB, por sus siglas en inglés) selló el adiós de los dos cubanos más mediáticos de la Liga Americana: el slugger Yordan Álvarez y el lanzador Aroldis Chapman.
Los Astros de Houston, de los que Yordan fue bujía a lo largo de la campaña, cayeron en apenas dos juegos ante los Medias Blancas de Chicago, mientras a los Medias Rojas de Chapman los frenaron en seco uno de los exequipos del cerrador holguinero: los Yankees en Nueva York.
Los Medias Blancas ganaron este miércoles 7-3 en Houston y completaron la barrida sobre los Astros. Así, dejaron sin opciones al tunero de seguir ensanchando la mejor campaña de su trayectoria, coronada con el liderazgo de bateo del circuito con promedio de .316, además de despachar 42 jonrones y luchar por la Triple Corona hasta el final del calendario regular.
Houston, we don’t have a problem pic.twitter.com/NmPM6SCndJ
— Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) October 1, 2026
Poco pudo aportar Yordan a la causa, al irse en blanco en cuatro visitas al plato. Con ello dejó su producción ofensiva en la postemporada en solo un imparable en los ocho turnos oficiales sumados por él en los dos choques disputados.
La suerte estuvo siempre del lado visitante, pues Chicago anotó cuatro veces en el primer episodio ante el abridor Hunter Brown, ayudado por errores defensivos. En lo adelante, los Astros solo pudieron responder con jonrones solitarios de José Altuve, Jeremy Peña y Cam Smith.
Este duelo era el de mayores expectativas entre los aficionados cubanos dada la presencia en el bando de Chicago del joven antesalista Miguel Vargas, quien tuvo su mejor temporada en la fase preliminar, pero no ha tenido un feliz estreno en la instancia decisiva.
El habanero volvió a fallar en cinco turnos, lo que, unido a un similar desempeño en el choque anterior, lo mantiene a la espera de su primer imparable en la postemporada.
Esta vez el protagonismo recayó en Chase Meidroth, autor de un vuelacercas de tres carreras, y en el bullpen encabezado por Erick Fedde y Jordan Hicks, quienes no permitieron hits en cuatro entradas combinadas para apuntalar la victoria de Anthony Kay.
3-RUN POSTSEASON HOMER FOR CHASE MEIDROTH! pic.twitter.com/39yNEWjiLt
— Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) September 30, 2026
Boston desarmado
En el Yankee Stadium, los dueños de casa complacieron a sus parciales con la segunda victoria seguida ante los Medias Rojas de Boston, esta por 9-2. El éxito dejó sin opciones de supervivencia a sus archienemigos históricos y marcó el cierre de temporada para su cerrador estrella Aroldis Chapman.
Max Fried trabajó seis entradas, con seis ponches y una carrera limpia, y fue respaldado por Cody Bellinger al conectar jonrón y producir cuatro anotaciones.
CODY BELLINGER THREE-RUN HOMER
IT’S 8-1 YANKEES! pic.twitter.com/gUQC8CJQb9
— MLB (@MLB) October 1, 2026
Luis García Jr. también firmó un significativo aporte al batear de 5-3 con otro vuelacercas, signo de la oportunidad de los bateadores del Bronx, quienes ligaron de 9-6 con corredores en posición de anotar.
Sonny Gray cargó con la derrota, que tampoco pudieron evitar varios relevistas, entre ellos Garrett Crochet y Garrett Whitlock.
Chapman, sin oportunidad de cerrar un juego ajustado en la serie de comodín, tuvo una entrada de actuación en la que ponchó a los tres bateadores que enfrentó.
Con ese despliegue se convirtió en el primer jugador nacido en Cuba con participación en 10 postemporadas de MLB, y en el segundo de Latinoamérica con 10 o más experiencias de este tipo, solo superado por el legendario panameño Mariano Rivera (16).
¡EL MISIL SIGUE HACIENDO HISTORIA! 🇨🇺
Aroldis Chapman se convierte en el 2do jugador nacido en Latinoamérica en participar en 10 diferentes #Postseason uniéndose a Mariano Rivera. pic.twitter.com/1VjtJcLAZO
— MLB Español (@mlbespanol) October 1, 2026
Además, con los tres ponches recetados llegó a 76 ponches en octubre, para colocarse en el listado histórico de relevistas por detrás de Rivera (110) y Kenley Jansen (94).
Con 38 años, el holguinero cerró una de sus mejores experiencias de las últimas temporadas. A lo largo del tramo regular fijó una efectividad de 1.92 carreras limpias por juego, con 35 salvamentos y 71 ponches en 51.2 entradas.
Sin Cachorros en juego
Las cosas también fueron bien en casa para los Padres de San Diego, al despachar por segunda ocasión sucesiva a los Cachorros de Chicago, esta vez con pizarra de 4-1.
Gavin Sheets conectó jonrón de dos carreras, al tiempo que Xander Bogaerts y Ty France aportaban dos hits cada uno.
Summer’s over, we’re on to October. pic.twitter.com/I4KRWqSyyf
— San Diego Padres (@Padres) October 1, 2026
La ocasión fue propicia para que el relevista cubano Adrián Morejón debutara en la serie lanzando dos entradas en blanco, con un hit permitido, sirviendo de puente hacia los cerrojos de Mason Miller y Jason Adam.
Todo lo contrario sucedió en Atlanta, donde los Filis de Filadelfia lograron equilibrar el pulso con una victoria 4-3 sellada en 10 entradas, que extendió hasta este jueves la definición del trámite.
Kyle Schwarber, Bryce Harper y Alec Bohm combinaron su poder con jonrones para la causa de los visitantes, mientras que el joven Andrew Painter retiraba a los bateadores de Atlanta durante tres entradas en blanco para quedarse con la victoria.
Well, that was wild pic.twitter.com/FpU4KdGxXo
— Philadelphia Phillies (@Phillies) September 30, 2026
El relevista cubano Raisel Iglesias trabajó un inning por los Bravos, con un hit permitido y sin tolerar carreras.
A la espera de esta decisión, los Medias Blancas se alistan para enfrentar a los Guardianes de Cleveland en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana, que arranca el venidero sábado 3 de octubre.
Por su parte, los Yankees enfrentarán con el mismo objetivo a los Rays de Tampa Bay, que cuentan en su filas con los cubanos con el cubano Yandy Díaz y Victor Mesa Jr.
En la Liga Nacional, San Diego pactó su choque con los Cerveceros de Milwaukee —el mejor equipo de la temporada regular con 103 victorias— y los actuales campeones, los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, con el cubano Andy Pagés entre sus referentes, aguardan para conocer su primer rival en la ruta hacia la conquista de su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva.

item.title: [mlb.com] Houston? No problem! White Sox end 21-year wait with sweep
item.dc:creator: Scott Merkin

item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON -- There was a moment with nobody out in the sixth inning Wednesday night during Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series that perfectly encapsulated the White Sox remarkable season and the downright fun they’ve had along the way.
Chase Meidroth connected on a three-run home run off Bryan Abreu, turning a one-run lead into a 7-3 advantage, which was ultimately the final score. But it was Meidroth’s reaction that reinforced the point.
Meidroth pumped his fist and screamed with joy from the moment he connected until he touched home plate, his emotions on full display. Back in the visitors’ clubhouse, the champagne was chilling as the White Sox prepared to take another somewhat unexpected step in the postseason.
“When I’m locked in on the field, I don’t know what goes through my mind,” Meidroth said. “All I’m thinking about is me and the baseball and trying to compete. But I had a good feeling.”
Good feelings have surrounded the White Sox since Spring Training, even dating back to SoxFest in late January. They’ve arguably been baseball’s best story in 2026, and perhaps one of the best in sports.
But this two-game sweep against the undermanned Astros proved they are a talented team to be reckoned with throughout the postseason. They are more than the young, energetic squad that shook off three consecutive 100-plus-loss campaigns to reach the playoffs.
Their second clubhouse celebration in a week -- and one of five they hope to have this postseason -- marked their first playoff series victory since 2005. That last series victory was a four-game sweep over the Astros in the World Series, with Games 3 and 4 played at what is now Daikin Park.
“These players are scared of nothing,” White Sox general manager Chris Getz said. “And whether it be myself or others, it’s like, 'How do we continue to nurture and fuel this group?'”
"We were able to do that with two games that I thought were emblematic of how we've won all season,” manager Will Venable said. “Contributions from everywhere. Sammy [Antonacci] setting the tone, great job down the lineup with everyone behind him. Guys pitching in different spots, going out whenever and getting the job done, and they did it."
For the second straight game, Chicago took control in the first inning with the help of Houston's poor defense. The White Sox scored four runs off Astros ace Hunter Brown, who had a 6-0 record with a 2.39 ERA over six career starts against the White Sox entering Wednesday.
Antonacci doubled on a line drive to left field that Yordan Alvarez seemed to have a play on but didn’t make. Kyle Teel singled home Antonacci, and Miguel Vargas reached on third baseman Nick Allen’s fielding error.
Andrew Benintendi singled home a second run, and when Lucas Spence's throw home got away from catcher Yainer Diaz, Vargas scored the third run. Tristan Peters then added an RBI single to cap the scoring in the opening frame.
Houston crept back with solo home runs from Jeremy Peña, Cam Smith and Jose Altuve off White Sox ace Sean Burke, who struck out eight over four innings. The Astros had a golden opportunity in the fifth inning, putting runners on first and second with one out for Alvarez. Anthony Kay was on the mound for his first true relief appearance this season.
Kay fell behind in the count, 3-0, threw a pitch in the zone that was taken by Alvarez and then got him to fly out to Antonacci in left on the next pitch. Isaac Paredes walked to load the bases, but Altuve flied out to right to end the frame.
Then Meidroth provided breathing room in the sixth, launching his three-run homer to restore Chicago’s four-run lead. Twelve outs stood between the White Sox and playoff history, but they had reasserted control, and Erick Fedde handled the final two innings to finish it off.
“You saw how it was this series,” Kay said. “Everyone didn't worry about themselves, just played as a team and did the best they could.”
“Hard to imagine myself in that situation, honestly, but I'm so glad they chose me with the ball and to give the team the win,” Fedde said. “This whole fan base deserved [this]. This whole organization deserved [this]. Feels good to move on to the next round.”
And now, it’s on to Cleveland and the AL Division Series for the White Sox, in the ongoing saga between AL Central rivals. The White Sox won the season series, 7-6, but the Guardians won the division by one game to earn home-field advantage.
Cleveland features a strong rotation and one of the best closers in the game in Cade Smith. Then again, the Guardians will see a team on a roll that has been 21 years in the making.

item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON -- Chase Meidroth hit a backbreaking three-run home run in the sixth inning to help the Chicago White Sox make a big early lead stand up in a 7-3 victory Wednesday against the Houston Astros that capped a two-game sweep of their American League wild-card series.
The White Sox earned their first postseason series victory since their sweep of the Astros in the 2005 World Series. The White Sox will face the Cleveland Guardians in a best-of-5 American League Division Series that begins Saturday in Cleveland.
“I’m really just happy for everybody over the last few years who experienced White Sox baseball when it obviously wasn’t at its best,” Chicago manager Will Venable said postgame. “It’s such a storied franchise. (White Sox owner) Jerry (Reinsdorf) put so much into this team, loves this team so much, and to be able to reward him and the city of Chicago, who have been in our corner and supported us from Day 1 that I’ve been there, just feels really good.
“I’m proud of the guys and certainly happy for them. They’re probably the only ones in this country that believed they could be in this spot, and they maintained that belief in the beginning of the season and went throughout the season maintaining that. They made it happen.”
The Astros returned to the playoffs after a one-year absence but have not advanced past the wild-card round since 2023.
“(Astros owner) Jim (Crane) has been very clear about his process and when he wants to have that conversation,” Houston manager Joe Espada, who finishes the season without an extension in place to stay with the Astros. “I respect the process and how blessed I’ve been to have been here for over nine years, experienced so many division titles, championship series, World Series -- winning one as a bench coach. As a manager, I have witnessed so many great moments. Obviously, I would like to continue enjoying those moments.”
After the Astros left the bases loaded in the fifth, Meidroth extended a 4-3 lead by driving a 3-1 slider from Astros reliever Bryan Abreu 390 feet to left-center field.
The White Sox scored four runs in the top of the first inning off Astros ace Hunter Brown (0-1), who didn’t make it out of the first as he allowed five hits, four runs (three earned) and one walk while the defense contributed two errors.
Kyle Teel, Andrew Benintendi and Tristan Peters recorded RBI singles in the first while Miguel Vargas reached on a fielding error by Astros third baseman Nick Allen and scored on a throwing error by center fielder Lucas Spence. Brown retired two of the nine batters he faced.
The Astros began a methodical climb back into the game in the bottom of the first when leadoff man Jeremy Pena smacked the first of three solo home runs off Chicago starter Sean Burke.
Pena drilled a 1-1 slider 395 feet to left-center field. An inning later, Cam Smith bashed a 1-0 sinker 440 feet to left field to close the margin to 4-2. In the fourth inning, Jose Altuve socked his 28th career postseason homer -- second all-time to Manny Ramirez -- to left to bring Houston within 4-3.
Burke allowed three runs and four hits while recording eight strikeouts in four innings. When the Astros built another serious threat in the fifth, White Sox left-hander Anthony Kay delivered.
After reliever Huascar Brazoban hit Cam Smith with a pitch and gave up a single to Pena, Kay (1-0) entered with one out and retired MVP candidate Yordan Alvarez on a deep fly just in front of the Crawford Boxes in left. Kay loaded the bases by walking Isaac Paredes but induced Altuve into a harmless flyout to right to end the inning.
Peter Lambert, the Astros’ third pitcher of the game, needed only 36 pitches to work three perfect innings, but he walked Benintendi and Peters to open the sixth. After Abreu entered the game, Meidroth faked a bunt that enabled pinch runner Luisangel Acuna and Peters to steal third and second base, respectively. With the infield in, Meidroth made it moot by crushing a hanging slider he immediately knew was a home run.

item.title: [Sportsnet.ca] White Sox chase Astros ace Hunter Brown in first inning of Game 2
item.dc:creator: Sportsnet Staff
item.description: After dropping Game 1 of their wild-card series to the Chicago White Sox while throwing a bullpen day, the Houston Astros had to feel a sense of relief knowing they were turning to their ace, Hunter Brown, for Game 2. But as the second inning came around on Wednesday, Brown had already been chased from the contest. item.content:encoded:
After dropping Game 1 of their wild-card series to the Chicago White Sox while throwing a bullpen day, the Houston Astros had to feel a sense of relief knowing they were turning to their ace, Hunter Brown, for Game 2.
But as the second inning came around on Wednesday, Brown had already been chased from the contest.
Chicago sent 10 batters to the plate in a four-run first, tagging Brown for five hits as it looked to win its first playoff series since 2005.
Brown managed to get two outs — both by way of the strikeout — before manager Joe Espada made the move to the bullpen.
White Sox leadoff hitter Sam Antonacci wasted little time putting Brown on his back foot, opening the game with a double that went off Astros left fielder Yordan Alvarez's glove. Kyle Teel then brought home Antonacci with a single, Miguel Vargas reached on an error, Andrew Benintendi scored both with a single and Tristan Peters completed the rally with an RBI single of his own.
Brown left with the bases loaded and two out, but Tuesday's opener, AJ Blubaugh, entered and escaped the jam.
Houston's pitching staff has been ravaged by injuries this season, leaving the 28-year-old Brown and Hayden Wesneski as their lone healthy starters for the playoffs.
With the Astros not clinching their AL West title until the final day of the regular season, they weren't able to line up their pitching staff, which led to the bullpen day in Game 1 before Brown and Wesneski could return on normal rest.
"Having those guys healthy with regular rest, it's super valuable for us," Espdada said before the series began, making Brown's short start all the more costly for an Astros team already needing length from their pitchers.
Brown finished the 2026 regular season with a 3.19 ERA and 124 strikeouts over 107.1 innings. He was also hit by the injury bug earlier in the season, which limited the six-foot-two right-hander to just 20 starts.

item.content:encoded:
The Astros, who roared back from an early-season deficit to win their eighth American League West title in 10 seasons Sunday, return to the playoffs following a one-year absence to face the upstart White Sox, who led the AL Central for much of the season before settling for the final Wild Spot in the AL.
While this series might not attract the attention of the AL’s other Wild Card Series -- the Yankees and Red Sox -- Astros-White Sox is an intriguing battle featuring a playoff-tested Houston team that has star power in AL Most Valuable Player favorite Yordan Alvarez, former World Series MVP Jeremy Peña and Jose Altuve, one of this generation’s greatest postseason performers, against a Chicago team with some up-and-coming stars.
“I feel like we did the hardest part, which was to get in,” Alvarez said.
The White Sox are led by Miguel Vargas and Munetaka Murakami, one of the best power-hitting duos in baseball. Murakami slammed 35 home runs as a rookie, and Vargas had 33 homers and should receive some downballot MVP votes.
"It feels good,” White Sox designated hitter Andrew Benintendi said. “I think that kind of hit a certain point of the year where you slot yourself in there. Now it’s officially over. The real season starts now."
When is the game and how can I watch it?
Game 1 of the White Sox-Astros Wild Card Series is underway at Daikin Park. The game is being broadcast on Peacock and NBCSN.
The Wild Card Series will be available in Spanish on Universo, while Univision Radio will provide Spanish language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB Postseason games, beginning with the Wild Card Series.
Who are the starting pitchers?
White Sox: Hagen Smith, LHP
Key Stats: 1.29 ERA, 28 IP, 13.1 K/9
With a chance to win the American League Central, the White Sox used Sean Burke (11-7, 3.34), Davis Martin (9-8, 3.95) and Anthony Kay (10-9, 4.44) against the last-place Rockies this weekend. Burke is likely lined up for Game 2 behind Game 1 starter Hagen Smith, who got the nod in an expected "bullpen-type game" from manager Will Venable on Monday. Smith is a largely untested rookie, but during his 18 games and 28 innings, he has induced some ugly-looking swings from the opposition.
Astros: AJ Blubaugh, RHP
Key Stats: Led MLB relievers with 96 IP
The 25-year-old rookie will start Tuesday’s Game 1 as the opener of what will be a bullpen game. Blubaugh threw 15 pitches in relief on Friday against the A’s, allowing one run in two-thirds of an inning.
Blubaugh led the Major Leagues with 27 relief appearances of at least two innings this season, the most by an Astros pitcher since Dave Veres had 27 in 1995. Blubaugh led all relievers with a career-high 96 innings. He has thrown more than two innings in only five games this season.
Blubaugh faced the White Sox three times in the regular season, allowing no runs, four hits and two walks while striking out three in four innings.
What are the starting lineups?
White Sox: With the Astros going with a bullpen game, the White Sox are trotting out this lineup.
Astros: The last three spots in the order are occupied by outfielders. Rookie Lucas Spence, who hit four homers in the season’s final series, earned the start in center, and Cam Smith will be in right field, hitting eighth.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
White Sox: Venable is not set on one lockdown closer, although Grant Taylor is coming off a dominant campaign with a 2.25 ERA and 106 strikeouts in 84 innings. So, Taylor could be used for two innings in the sixth and seventh, or try to finish off a victory in the ninth. The same holds true for relievers such as Sean Newcomb, Bryan Hudson and the rookie additions of Smith and Noah Schultz.
Astros: A seven-inning outing by starter Hayden Wesneski on Saturday and Sunday’s blowout win in the regular-season finale have Houston’s bullpen in really good shape heading into the postseason, especially with the Astros contemplating a bullpen game for Tuesday. They could get multiple innings out of the bullpen from Josh Hendrickson, Miguel Ullola and AJ Blubaugh in an effort to get the ball to setup man Bryan Abreu and closer Josh Hader, who finished the season with a 1.01 ERA and 26-for-26 in save chances. He hasn’t pitched since Wednesday.
Any injuries of note?
White Sox: Chase Meidroth has been dealing with left hamstring discomfort, among myriad nagging injuries. He sat out most of the weekend against the Rockies after leaving early from Thursday’s playoff-clincher in Kansas City, but should be available Tuesday.
Astros: Isaac Paredes fouled a ball off his knee Saturday in West Sacramento and was in the lineup for Sunday’s season finale, but the Astros were so concerned about the knee that they called up infielder Raynel Delgado to give them some coverage at third base. Center fielders Daulton Varsho (wrist) and Brice Matthews (knee) both landed on the IL last week, so neither will be available for the Wild Card Series.
Who is hot and who is not?
White Sox: Colson Montgomery was a deserving All-Star candidate who was passed over, but has found rough going since the break. In fact, Montgomery finished the season with a .197 average and set the single-season Major League record with 227 strikeouts. He spoke eloquently pregame Sunday about being focused on doing anything to help the team and looking for a reset starting with the playoffs.
Miguel Vargas’ season has been a revelation overall, with 33 homers, 31 doubles, 22 stolen bases, 101 walks, 93 RBIs and 106 runs scored. Munetaka Murakami also seems back on track, with his 35 homers tying Ron Kittle for the second-highest single-season home run total for a White Sox rookie trailing only Jose Abreu (36 in 2014).
Astros: Yordan Alvarez won the AL batting title and will likely add his first AL Most Valuable Player to his resume following a season in which he slashed .316/.432/.601 with 105 runs, 34 doubles, 42 homers, 106 RBIs and 109 walks. Jeremy Peña slashed .353/.358/.706 with five homers and nine RBIs in the Astros’ final 12 games.
Christian Walker had a 1.167 OPS with four homers in the last eight games, Yainer Diaz slashed .350/.377/.581 with six homers and 17 RBIs in 34 games since Aug. 16 and rookie Lucas Spence was 6-for-15 with four homers, a triple and nine RBIs in the final four games of the season.
Taylor Trammell finished the season 0-for-20.
Anything else fans might want to know?
• The Astros have lost seven consecutive home playoff games, dating to 2023.
• This is the third time the Astros and White Sox have met in the playoffs. The White Sox swept Houston in the 2005 World Series, and the Astros eliminated the White Sox in four games in the 2021 ALDS.

item.content:encoded:
The Houston Astros enter the postseason with the AL MVP favorite in their lineup.
Yordan Alvarez should be considered the most feared hitter in baseball for this year's playoffs.
But the rest of Houston's lineup has been mediocre at best.
"The Astros have the presumptive AL MVP in Yordan Alvarez, but the rest of the offense has produced a .233/.300/.396 line this year," Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter wrote. "He will need to replicate his memorable performance in the 2023 ALCS for pretty much the entirety of October."
Clearly, the Astros rely on Alvarez to do most of their offensive damage, but he may not be the AL West club's "X-Factor" during the Wild Card Series against the Chicago White Sox.
Instead, Reuter has tabbed rookie center fielder Lucas Spence as someone who can help Houston make a deep postseason run.
"Lucas Spence went 6-for-18 with four home runs in five games after being recalled from Triple-A when [Daulton] Varsho and [Brice] Matthews were placed on the injured list," Reuter added. "He suddenly looks like the no-doubt starting center fielder for the club's playoff run."
MORE: Pirates urged to re-sign Brandon Lowe if they ‘want to be taken seriously’
Varsho is unavailable in the Wild Card Series due to left wrist inflammation caused by cysts.
He is a Gold Glove outfielder but has hit poorly following a midseason trade from the Toronto Blue Jays.
Spence has just 19 MLB games under his belt but looks up for the challenge, hitting the first three home runs of his career in a single game during the last week of the regular season against the Athletics.

item.content:encoded:
The postseason field is finally set. After Sunday’s results on the final day of the regular season, we officially know what 12 teams will be in contention for the 2026 World Series.
The Diamondbacks, despite their late push, fell short of the playoffs, thanks to a Phillies win on Sunday against the Rays. Meanwhile, the final domino to fall in the American League went in favor of the Astros, who secured the AL West title with a victory over the Athletics on Sunday. Houston becomes the worst team to ever make the playoffs in a 162-game season, sneaking in and winning the division with just an 81–81 record.
Fans won’t have to wait long for postseason to get underway, with the Wild Card series set to begin on Tuesday. But before the action gets going, we’re going to do a final power ranking, assessing where all 12 teams sit and detailing their biggest strength and weakness.
1. Los Angeles Dodgers
Biggest strength: Elite starting pitching, lineup
Biggest weakness: Bullpen
The Dodgers may be the No. 2 seed in the National League, but they’re built to win in October. It’s hard to determine what’s a greater strength between their loaded starting rotation or their star-studded lineup. There’s no weaknesses in their rotation, with All-Star caliber pitchers available to take the mound every night, even with Shohei Ohtani restricted to DH duties. There isn’t a team in MLB with more postseason experience than Los Angeles, who have won back-to-back World Series with this core. During the regular season, the Dodgers had MLB’s second-highest OPS (.762) and fourth-best ERA (3.55). If there’s any way to beat them it’s by getting after a bullpen that has been inconsistent throughout the season, though it’s still a top-10 unit. Injuries have plagued their relief pitching corps, however, with the likes of Blake Treinen, Edgardo Henriquez and Will Klein all currently on IL.
2. Milwaukee Brewers
Biggest strength: Elite pitching
Biggest weakness: Lack of power
The Brewers’ rotation, headlined by NL Cy Young favorite Jacob Misiorowski, has been one of MLB’s best, and it’s helped the team secure the league’s best regular-season record. The starting rotation owns MLB’s fifth-best ERA (3.65) and their bullpen has been equally impressive, ranking third in MLB with a 3.40 ERA. Milwaukee has scored the second-most runs in the league this season (832), as their small-ball approach has worked wonders for them. But in October, when a single swing of the bat can dramatically change a team’s fortunes and rallies are harder to come by, they might not have the power hitters capable of providing that big home run swing. The Brewers didn’t have a single 30-home run hitter this season and had just three everyday starters with a slugging percentage above .450.
3. Tampa Bay Rays
Biggest strength: Elite starting pitching
Biggest weakness: Bottom-third of the lineup
The Rays had the best record in the American League this season, largely thanks to their pitching. The starting rotation has been excellent, ranking third in MLB with a 3.51 ERA. Drew Rasmussen has quietly been one of MLB’s best arms, and Freddy Peralta has begun to rediscover his previous form after a rough go with the Mets and a shaky start on the mound in Tampa. Much like the Brewers, the Rays primarily utilize a small-ball approach offensively. The Rays hit the ninth-fewest home runs in MLB this year, and despite rostering some elite hitters such as Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz, they haven’t received much production out of the bottom third of their lineup, which is their biggest weakness with the postseason looming.
4. Atlanta Braves
Biggest strength: Deep lineup
Biggest weakness: Plate discipline, low on-base rates
The Braves are another team with an abundance of postseason experience in the lineup. They have several players that can turn a game on its head with one swing of the bat, and had five 20-plus home run hitters during the regular season in Matt Olson, Michael Harris, Drake Baldwin, Ozzie Albies and Ronald Acuña Jr. Although the lineup is flush with talent, the group has a tendency to chase pitches out of the zone, and they don’t draw walks at a high rate. The Braves ranked 28th in MLB in on-base percentage (.309) during the regular season, often opting for an aggressive approach at the plate rather than a patient one. That could prove costly in October against some of the best pitchers in the sport, where slowing the game down and getting runners on base by any means necessary will be crucial.
5. New York Yankees
Biggest strength: Elite pitching rotation
Biggest weakness: Offense (without Aaron Judge), high strikeout rates
Yankees starting pitchers led MLB with a 3.30 ERA this season, and they’ll have one of the best rotations in the postseason with Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodon set to take the mound in October. The bullpen has been a bit inconsistent, but they should be able to ride their starting rotation deep into games. The biggest weakness for the Yankees is their lineup, particularly without Aaron Judge in the mix. New York had the sixth-most strikeouts this season and were tied for 11th in MLB with a .720 OPS. With Judge out of the lineup, however, their OPS falls to a .690 mark, which would be 29th in MLB.
6. San Diego Padres
Biggest strength: Elite bullpen
Biggest weakness: Starting pitching
The Padres’ bullpen has been as reliable as they come this season, and the team flexes multiple elite relievers who they can reliably turn the ball over to in the later innings in Mason Miller, Yuki Matsui and Adrian Morejon, among others. San Diego has shaken off a slow start to the year and are playing at an extremely high level heading into the postseason. The offense is alive again after a dreadful first couple of months of the season, with players like Fernando Tatis Jr. and Jackson Merrill having been among MLB’s best second-half performers at the plate. The starting pitching will be the x-factor in October, however. With Casey Mize landing on the IL, their options in the rotation are even thinner. Remaining competitive within the first six innings will be crucial for the Padres, whose starting pitchers rank 21st in MLB with a 4.42 ERA this year.
7. Chicago Cubs
Biggest strength: Dominant lineup
Biggest weakness: Starting pitching
The Cubs have had MLB’s best offense this season, leading the league in OPS (.767), walks (674), runs scored (850) and slugging percentage (.428). They’ve been particularly elite since the All-Star break, logging a .797 OPS in their last 66 games. With Pete Crow-Armstrong playing at an MVP level and Alex Bregman having enjoyed a monster second half, the Cubs’ offense will be tough to shut down in October. Of course, they’ll need their pitching to live up to their end of the bargain, which it’s struggled to do this season. Chicago’s starting pitching has been disappointing and plagued by injuries. The starting rotation ranks 18th in MLB with a 4.27 ERA this year and have surrendered the third-most home runs (142).
8. Boston Red Sox
Biggest strength: Elite pitching
Biggest weakness: Inconsistent offense
The Red Sox’s pitching as a whole has been excellent. Boston’s bullpen owns a league-best 3.00 ERA this season, and no group of relievers in MLB has surrendered fewer home runs (55). Their starters have been great, too, ranking eighth in the league with a 3.92 ERA, and they boast a solid mix of veterans (Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez) and young, emerging starters (Payton Tolle and Jake Bennett). Offensively, however, the Red Sox have been prone to spells of inconsistency. They started the season ice cold before enjoying a scalding hot summer streak, but they’ve come crashing back down to earth in the final month of the season. The Red Sox rank dead last in MLB in OPS (.651) throughout the month of September, and they’re batting a league-worst .219 in that span.
9. Cleveland Guardians
Biggest strength: Starting pitching
Biggest weakness: Lack of power
The Guardians starting pitching has been a top-10 unit this season, ranking ninth in ERA (3.93) and fifth in strikeouts (878). Parker Messick has been superb in his first full season in MLB, and Gavin Williams has emerged as one of the league’s best strikeout pitchers. Cleveland will feel confident with those two spearheading the rotation, but they may struggle to get the run support required to take advantage of their quality starters. The Guardians rank 24th in MLB with 678 runs scored, 26th in OPS (.696) and 27th in home runs (162) this season. If they can’t come up with some big at-bats, it won’t matter how effective their pitching is in October.
10. Philadelphia Phillies
Biggest strength: Starting pitching
Biggest weakness: Defense, bullpen
The Phillies have one of the best starting rotations in MLB, but they’ve been plagued by some underperforming position players and a lackluster bullpen. There’s arguably no better trio of starters in MLB than Cristopher Sánchez, Zack Wheeler and Jesús Luzardo. The team’s starting rotation ranks seventh in the league with a 3.80 ERA, but their bullpen ranks 21st in ERA (4.43). Defensively, the Phillies have been atrocious, too. Only the Athletics have fewer defensive runs saved than the Phillies’ -43, according to the Fielding Bible, and the infield has been a serious concern, with Trea Turner, Bryce Harper and Alec Bohm all ranking among the bottom 26 defensive players (of 270 qualified players) in MLB in terms of outs above average, per Statcast. Defensive shortcomings and mishaps could prove highly costly in October, and that’s an area that’s plagued Philadelphia all season.
11. Chicago White Sox
Biggest strength: Power hitting
Biggest weakness: Starting pitching
The White Sox have a potent lineup and are the only team in MLB that have three players who hit 30 or more home runs in Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami and Colson Montgomery. Chicago hit the fifth-most home runs this season (211) and scored the fifth-most runs (776). While the offense is among the league’s best in terms of power, the White Sox starting pitching is a serious concern. The starting rotation posted a season ERA of 4.60 (fourth-worst in MLB), a 1.34 WHIP (sixth-worst in MLB) and recorded the third-fewest strikeouts of any starting rotation in the league. Chicago’s starters also threw the fewest innings in MLB this season, often struggling to get deep into games before the baton was passed to the bullpen. If the starting rotation can’t keep runs off the board, it might not matter how explosive their lineup can be.
12. Houston Astros
Biggest strength: Power hitting
Biggest weakness: Starting pitching
Yordan Alvarez is likely to win the AL MVP, and he’s the type of hitter teams will not be eager to pitch to in October. No team in MLB hit more home runs than the Astros, who hit 226. In addition to Alvarez’s 42, Houston had four other players with 20-plus homers, including Christian Walker (29), Isaac Paredes (25), Jeremy Peña (22) and Cam Smith (21). They don’t have much to worry about offensively, but their lineup will need to produce in order to ease the burden on their starting rotation, which has largely struggled this year. Hunter Brown remains a reliable ace, but beyond him there’s a lack of experience and talent within the rotation. Astros starters ranked 27th in MLB with a 4.81 ERA and 1.40 WHIP, both of which were the worst among all teams that qualified for the postseason, and they walked the most batters in MLB this season. If the lineup can’t make up for the rotation’s shortcomings, it could be a short postseason stint for Houston this year.
Karl Rasmussen is a staff writer for Sports Illustrated. A University of Oregon alum who joined SI in February 2023, his work has appeared on 12up and ClutchPoints. Rasmussen is a loyal Tottenham, Jets, Yankees and Ducks fan.

item.title: [Claro Sports] El poder latino hace historia en MLB con los títulos de bateo de Yordan Álvarez y Gabriel Moreno
item.dc:creator: Julian Castillo
item.description: Los títulos de bateo de MLB 2026 quedaron en manos de latinos demostrando su peso en la liga Lostítulos de bateo de la temporada regular de MLB 2026 quedaron en manos de dos figuras latinas. Yordan Álvarez, de los Astros de Houston, conquistó el reconocimiento de la Liga Americana con promedio de .316, mientras Gabriel Moreno, receptor de los Diamondbacks de Arizona, ganó el de la Liga Nacional tras batear para .311. Los títulos de bateo de Yordan Álvarez y Gabriel Moreno respondieron a dos reco
item.content:encoded:
Los títulos de bateo de MLB 2026 quedaron en manos de latinos demostrando su peso en la liga
Lostítulos de bateo de la temporada regular de MLB 2026 quedaron en manos de dos figuras latinas. Yordan Álvarez, de los Astros de Houston, conquistó el reconocimiento de la Liga Americana con promedio de .316, mientras Gabriel Moreno, receptor de los Diamondbacks de Arizona, ganó el de la Liga Nacional tras batear para .311.
Los títulos de bateo de Yordan Álvarez y Gabriel Moreno respondieron a dos recorridos distintos, aunque igual de consistentes. El cubano sostuvo un contacto sólido durante casi toda la temporada y mantuvo su promedio entre los más altos de la Liga Americana. Moreno, por su parte, superó un inicio complicado, encontró regularidad en la segunda mitad del calendario y sostuvo una disputa cerrada con su compatriota Luis Arráez hasta el último día de la campaña.
La buena temporada de los latinos con el madero no se limita a los casos de Álvarez y Moreno. Cuatro de los cinco mejores bateadores de toda MLB fueron latinos y cada uno superó el .300 de promedio. Álvarez, Moreno, Luis Arráez y Otto López compartieron la parte alta de una lista que confirma el peso que tienen los hispanos en la liga.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Luis Arráez, entre los mejores bateadores de las Grandes Ligas, aparece como el nombre caliente de la fecha límite de cambios
¿Cómo fue la temporada de Yordan Álvarez en 2026?
Yordan Álvarez firmó una campaña completa con los Astros de Houston y se quedó con su primer título de bateo al terminar con promedio de .316. El jardinero designado cubano disputó 158 juegos, sumó 179 hits en 567 turnos, anotó 105 carreras, conectó 34 dobles, pegó 42 jonrones y produjo 106 carreras. Su línea ofensiva quedó en .316/.432/.601, con un OPS de 1.033, el mejor de toda la MLB.
El título tuvo un valor especial porque Álvarez no dependió solo del cuadrangular. Sus 109 boletos muestran una disciplina poco habitual en un bateador de tanto poder y ayudaron a que llegara a base con frecuencia. En un contexto de ofensivas menos cargadas de promedios altos, su .316 representó el promedio más bajo de un líder global de MLB desde 1968, aunque eso no reduce el tamaño de su producción general.
Todo este aporte ofensivo fue decisivo en la clasificación de Houston los playoffs. Los Astros alcanzaron la postemporada con Álvarez como una de sus piezas ofensivas principales y con argumentos sólidos para entrar en la conversación por el Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana. MLB también lo ubicó como colíder de la Americana en WAR, con 6.8, junto a Bobby Witt Jr.
Para la franquicia texana, el premio amplía una secuencia que ya incluye a José Altuve, ganador en 2014, 2016 y 2017, y a Yuli Gurriel, líder de bateo en 2021. Álvarez se convirtió en el tercer Astro que obtiene el reconocimiento desde 2014.
¿Cómo fue la temporada de Gabriel Moreno en 2026?
Gabriel Moreno conquistó el primer título de bateo en la historia de los Diamondbacks de Arizona. El receptor venezolano cerró con .311 de promedio, producto de 147 hits en 473 turnos, con 33 dobles, un triple, 16 jonrones, 83 carreras impulsadas y 72 anotadas en 130 juegos. Su línea final fue de .311/.388/.486, acompañada por un OPS de .874.
Moreno superó por apenas un punto a Luis Arráez, quien terminó con .310 para los Phillies. La definición tuvo peso hasta la última jornada y puso al receptor de Arizona en una categoría poco común. Moreno se convirtió en el primer catcher titular que gana una corona de bateo desde Buster Posey en 2012.
La campaña de Moreno tomó fuerza después de un arranque marcado por una lesión en el oblicuo izquierdo. Pasó gran parte de abril en la lista de lesionados y llegó a junio por debajo de .250. Desde el 7 de junio, el venezolano bateó .332, una recuperación que cambió el rumbo de su temporada y lo llevó al liderato de la Liga Nacional.
A diferencia de Álvarez, en el caso del venezolano su buena actuación con el madero no fue suficiente para poder ayudar a su equipo para poder conseguir un pase a los playoffs. Arizona terminó como tercero del oeste de la Liga Nacional por detrás de Los Angeles Dodgers y los San Diego Padres, al tiempo que cerraron a 3 juegos de distancia del boleto de Wild Card.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Calendario de playoffs MLB 2026: Fechas, horarios y cómo ver la postemporada completa en español
¿Cuántas veces dos latinos han ganado los títulos de bateo de MLB?
- 1964
- Liga Americana: Tony Oliva, Mellizos de Minnesota, .323.
- Liga Nacional: Roberto Clemente, Piratas de Pittsburgh, .339.
- 1965
- Liga Americana: Tony Oliva, Mellizos de Minnesota, .321.
- Liga Nacional: Roberto Clemente, Piratas de Pittsburgh, .329.
- 2011
- Liga Americana: Miguel Cabrera, Tigres de Detroit, .344.
- Liga Nacional: Carlos González, Rockies de Colorado, .336.
- 2023
- Liga Americana: Yandy Díaz, Rays de Tampa Bay, .330.
- Liga Nacional: Luis Arráez, Marlins de Miami, .354.
- 2026
- Liga Americana: Yordan Álvarez, Astros de Houston, .316.
- Liga Nacional: Gabriel Moreno, Diamondbacks de Arizona, .311.

item.title: [MLB.com] Pete Alonso of the Baltimore Orioles named American League Player of the Week; Nolan Arenado of the Arizona Diamondbacks named National League Player of the Week

item.content:encoded:
First baseman Pete Alonso of the Baltimore Orioles has been named the American League Player of the Week, and third baseman Nolan Arenado of the Arizona Diamondbacks has been selected the National League Player of the Week. The announcements were made earlier today on MLB Network.
Alonso earned the honor for the seventh time in his career and second time this season after winning his first award in the AL with the Orioles on August 17th. He previously won five times during his tenure with the New York Mets, including June 24, 2019; September 26, 2022; July 30, 2023; April 15, 2024; and June 9, 2025. Alonso is the 12th player ever to garner honors in at least five consecutive seasons, regardless of team or league, joining Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero (8 seasons, 1998-2005); Manny Ramirez (7 seasons, 1997-2003); Arenado (6 seasons, 2014-2019); Aaron Judge (6 seasons, 2020-2025); George Bell (5 seasons, 1986-1990); Miguel Cabrera (5 seasons, 2012-2016); Hall of Famer Andre Dawson (5 seasons, 1987-1991); Carlos Delgado (5 seasons, 2000-2004); Clayton Kershaw (5 seasons, 2011-2015); Albert Pujols (5 seasons, 2005-2009); and Gary Sheffield (5 seasons, 1992-96). Arenado earned his ninth career award and first as a member of the Diamondbacks, marking Arizona’s fourth award of the year in addition to his teammates Ildemaro Vargas (April 27th); Ketel Marte (May 26th) and Corbin Carroll (August 17th). Arenado previously won six times as a member of the Colorado Rockies between 2014-2019 and twice as a member of the St. Louis Cardinals in 2022, including August 24, 2014; June 28, 2015; April 18, 2016; July 24, 2017; June 25, 2018; May 27, 2019; April 11, 2022; and August 8, 2022. He is the 31st player with at least nine awards in his career and just the eighth with at least nine awards in the National League, joining Barry Bonds (15); Pujols (13); Hall of Famer Mike Piazza (12); Sammy Sosa (11); Freddie Freeman (10); Hall of Famer Tony Gwynn (10); and Sheffield (9).
- The 31-year-old hit .389 (7-for-18) with five homers, eight RBI, three walks, eight runs scored, a 1.222 slugging percentage and a .500 on-base percentage across five contests.
- The Tampa, Florida native led the Majors in homers, slugging, OPS (1.722) and total bases (22); ranked second in runs scored; tied for third in RBI; and tied for fifth in on-base percentage.
- The five-time All-Star opened his week with a two-homer game against the Blue Jays on Monday and hit a pair of longballs in the first game of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium on Friday. Alonso now has 29 career multi-homer games which are third-most in the Majors since his debut in 2019 behind only Aaron Judge (40 G) and Kyle Schwarber (36 G).
- The 2019 Jackie Robinson NL Rookie of the Year also slugged a home run in the first game of a doubleheader on Wednesday against Toronto as he finished his year with 43 homers and 113 RBI. Per Elias, he became the first player since RBI became official in 1920 to lead the AL and NL in RBI for a single season after he led the NL with 131 RBI in 2022. Additionally, he is the eighth Orioles player to lead the league in RBI and the first since Chris Davis had 138 RBI in 2013.
- The 2025 Silver Slugger crossed the 40-homer threshold with his two-homer game on Monday, marking his fourth season of at least 40 home runs, joining 2019 (53 HR); 2022 (40 HR); and 2023 (46 HR). His 43 homers are third-most by a Baltimore player in their first season with the club, behind Hall of Famer Frank Robinson (49 HR in 1966) and Mark Trumbo (47 HR in 2016). Alonso, who has played in 577 consecutive games since June 18, 2023, became the first Oriole to start every game of a season since Jonathan Schoop in 2016.
- The 35-year-old hit .435 (10-for-23) with three homers, eight RBI, two doubles, two walks, seven runs scored, a stolen base, a .913 slugging percentage and a .519 on-base percentage in six games.
- The Newport Beach, California native tied for second in total bases (21) and hits; ranked third in on-base percentage and OPS (1.432); tied for third in slugging, RBI and runs scored; and tied for fifth in batting average.
- The eight-time All-Star slugged a homer on Tuesday and Thursday at Colorado before also going deep on Friday at San Diego, marking his 30th homer of the year. It marked the eighth time in his career that he hit at least 30 homers, and his eight seasons of at least 30 home runs are third-most by a primary third baseman (min. 100 GS at 3B in season), behind only Hall of Famers Mike Schmidt (12 seasons of 30+ HR) and Eddie Mathews (10 seasons of 30+ HR).
- The 10-time Rawlings Gold Glover and six-time Platinum Glove Award winner finished his season on a 13-game hitting streak that dates back to September 13th, and he hit safely in 18 of his final 20 games of the season. During the stretch, he slashed .420/.463/.840 with six homers, 16 RBI and a 1.303 OPS. Arenado’s hitting streak is the fourth-longest by a Diamondbacks player to end a season, trailing only Paul Goldschmidt (19 G in 2013); Chad Tracy (14 G in 2005); and Tony Womack (14 G in 1999).
- The five-time Silver Slugger reached base safely in each of his last 21 games, matching Luis Gonzalez (2001) for the longest streak to end a season in franchise history. Overall, his 21-game on-base streak is the fifth-longest single season on-base streak of his career behind a 30-game streak in 2014, a 25-gamer in 2024 and a pair of 24-gamers in 2024 and 2018.
Other noteworthy NL performances last week included starting pitcher Jared Jones (1-0, 0.00 ERA, 2 GS, 11.0 IP, 2 H, 0 BB, 14 SO) of the Pittsburgh Pirates; starting pitcher Eury Pérez (1-0, 0.00 ERA, 1 GS, 10.0 IP, 1 H, 1 BB, 11 SO) of the Miami Marlins; infielder Bryson Stott (.474, 2 RBI, 6 2B, 5 BB, 4 R, .789 SLG, .583 OBP) of the Philadelphia Phillies; rookie outfielder Carson Benge (.440, 1 HR, 4 RBI, 3 2B, 3 BB, 5 R, .680 SLG, .500 OBP) of the New York Mets; second baseman Brice Turang (.360, 2 HR, 7 RBI, 3 2B, 1 BB, 5 R, .720 SLG) and outfielder Jackson Chourio (.471, 1 HR, 5 RBI, 3 BB, 7 R, 2 SB, .647 SLG, .550 OBP) of the Milwaukee Brewers; the 2026 Tony Gwynn NL Batting Champion, catcher Gabriel Moreno (.400, 1 HR, 8 RBI, 1 2B, 1 3B, 2 BB, 5 R, .600 SLG, .435 OBP) of the Arizona Diamondbacks; and utilityman Mauricio Dubón (.368, 1 HR, 3 RBI, 1 BB, 3 R, 1 SB, .526 SLG, .400 OBP) of the Atlanta Braves.
Other noteworthy AL performances last week included rookie outfielder Lucas Spence (.333, 4 HR, 9 RBI, 1 2B, 1 3B, 4 BB, 5 R, 1.167 SLG, .455 OBP), the 2026 AL Rod Carew Batting Champion, All-Star outfielder Yordan Alvarez (.375, 2 HR, 7 RBI, 2 2B, 4 BB, 7 R, .708 SLG, .483 OBP) and first baseman Christian Walker (.348, 4 HR, 7 RBI, 1 2B, 3 BB, 7 R, .913 SLG, .407 OBP); utilityman Luke Keaschall (.381, 1 HR, 6 RBI, 2 2B, 1 3B, 3 BB, 10 R, 1 SB, .905 SLG, .462 OBP) of the Minnesota Twins; closer Cade Smith (0.00 ERA, 3 G, 2 SV, 2.2 IP, 0 H, 1 BB, 4 SO) of the Cleveland Guardians; first baseman Vinnie Pasquantino (.333, 3 HR, 9 RBI, 2 2B, 1 BB, 6 R, .792 SLG, .385 OBP) and outfielder Jac Caglianone (.455, 4 RBI, 5 2B, 4 R, .682 SLG, .455 OBP) of the Kansas City Royals; outfielder Wade Meckler (.435, 2 RBI, 1 2B, 3 BB, 3 R, .565 SLG, .480 OBP) of the Los Angeles Angels; and All-Star first baseman Munetaka Murakami (.292, 3 HR, 7 RBI, 2 2B, 2 BB, 5 R, .750 SLG, .370 OBP) and second baseman Chase Meidroth (.615, 1 HR, 5 RBI, 2 2B, 1 BB, 3 R, 1.000 SLG, .643 OBP) of the Chicago White Sox.
Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuña Jr. earned his fourth career Play of the Week Award, after previously winning on August 19, 2019; August 8, 2022; and July 21, 2025. Overall, it is the 13th honor for the Braves since the inception of the award in 2019 with Acuña’s four awards joined by honors to Charlie Culberson (7/8/2019); Nick Markakis (7/15/2019); Adam Duvall (9/8/2020); Tyler Matzek (5/10/2021); a joint award to Ozzie Albies and Orlando Arcia (7/3/2023); Austin Riley (8/19/2024); Michael Harris II (9/3/2024); Jurickson Profar (8/11/2025); and Jim Jarvis (5/11/2026). With no outs and the Braves leading the Marlins 1-0 in the second inning, Heriberto Hernández hit a ball towards the wall as Acuña made a leaping catch to take away extra-bases. Additional Play of the Week candidates included Javier Sanoja’s fantastic play to keep the game alive; Henry Bolte’s diving catch; Bryan Reynolds’ diving catch and throw to second for a double play; Ceddanne Rafaela’s diving catch; and Jase Bowen’s leaping catch at the wall.

item.content:encoded:
For the 14th straight year, the Dodgers are postseason-bound.
Winners of three of the past six World Series, the Dodgers are looking to continue their reign. The back-to-back defending champions are bidding for the Major Leagues' first three-peat since the Yankees won three straight titles from 1998-2000.
The Dodgers, the No. 2 seed in the National League, are just about at full strength now that the likes of Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki have returned from the injured list, but there are several other compelling storylines to follow before the postseason.
Here's what to watch as the NL West-champion Dodgers forge their path back to the Fall Classic:
What could the postseason roster look like?
The strength of the Dodgers' pitching staff is the rotation, so expect them to carry more starters than they need and get creative with using some of them in relief. Manager Dave Roberts indicated that the team may carry only 12 pitchers to make room for an additional position player on the bench in the NL Division Series.
It may be premature to pencil in Josue De Paula, as the organization’s top prospect has played in only 11 big league games. But the Dodgers liked what they saw, and he could be an impact lefty bat off the bench.
Catchers (2): Will Smith, Hunter Feduccia
First baseman (1): Freddie Freeman
Second baseman (1): Tommy Edman
Shortstop (1): Mookie Betts
Third baseman (1): Max Muncy
Outfielders (3): Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker
Utility/bench (3): Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim
Two-way player (1): Shohei Ohtani
Starters (4): Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Relievers (9): Edwin Díaz, Tanner Scott, Edgardo Henriquez, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Roki Sasaki, Kris Bubic, Brock Stewart
When does the postseason begin?
The NL Division Series begin on Saturday.
Who could be the Dodgers' NLDS opponent? 
The Dodgers won their 13th NL West title in the past 14 seasons and secured a first-round bye, so they will play the winner of the Wild Card Series between the Braves and the Phillies.
Against which teams do the Dodgers have home-field advantage?
The Dodgers have home-field advantage over every team in the postseason field except the Brewers, who finished the regular season with the best record in the Majors.
What will the postseason rotation look like?
Yamamoto, Skubal, Snell and Glasnow make up this year's Big Four. The rotation order is yet to be determined. One consideration is that Yamamoto is accustomed to starting on at least five days' rest, whereas the other three are comfortable starting on four days' rest. That makes Yamamoto likely to start Game 1 of the NLDS because he would be available for a potential Game 5 on his normal rest. 
What's the latest on Ohtani's status?
Ohtani was activated from the 15-day IL and hit in the Dodgers' final five games, going 5-for-21 (.238) with eight strikeouts and one walk. Roberts described the performance as Ohtani showing some rust and said the team does not have any health concerns with him. 
Which injured players could return?   
The Dodgers hope that Henriquez, who has emerged as an important leverage arm, can return for the postseason after his regular season came to a premature end due to lower back discomfort. He will face hitters during the bye week, and as long as he comes away feeling good, he will be activated for the NLDS.
Which roster spots may be up for grabs?
The final spot on the bench is far from set in stone. The Dodgers could carry De Paula, but Dalton Rushing, Alex Call and Hyeseong Kim are additional options. This decision could come down to whether they want to use that bench spot on a potential impact bat or someone who brings enhanced speed and/or defense to the table. If L.A. carries fewer than 13 pitchers, that would open an additional bench spot.
The bullpen should also have some openings. If Henriquez does not recover in time for the postseason, that opens an additional spot. Justin Wrobleski, Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan were starters for most of the season, but they will be relief options in the postseason. But Wrobleski was inconsistent in the second half, and the Dodgers have other left-handers who may be more reliable in leverage, such as Bubic.
Who will close out games?
Díaz was supposed to resolve the Dodgers' ninth-inning troubles, but he has only added to them in his first year in L.A. Since returning from the IL, he has looked much better, which could have him back in the mix to close out games. The Dodgers may be more likely to play the matchups instead of going with a set closer in the postseason. Based on regular-season performance, Scott and Henriquez are two of the top options to pitch in save situations. Perhaps Sasaki could reprise his postseason closer role if needed.
