item.content:encoded:
Red Sox move Sunday's game and will play doubleheader against Cubs on Friday with storm expected
CHICAGO -- Major League Baseball's postseason is rapidly approaching.
The Chicago Cubs and White Sox are among teams who had a chance to clinch a playoff spot Wednesday evening, but they both lost their games.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are seeking a third straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game's biggest stars will be able to participate in the playoffs, though.
The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they'll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angeles is rolling into the postseason and four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup on Wednesday after a stint on the injured list.
The New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves have also clinched spots in the postseason. Yankees slugger Aaron Judge, a three-time AL MVP, is dealing with a right calf strain that will likely keep him out through at least the Wild Card Series.
While the 12-team playoff field appears mostly set, there are a few long-shot contenders for the postseason, and specific matchups are in flux.
Here's some of what to watch as the season comes to a close.
Here's who can clinch a playoff spot Wednesday
In the American League, the Cleveland Guardians can qualify for the postseason with a win at Boston and a loss by either the Texas Rangers or Houston Astros.
The Chicago White Sox can cap a turnaround season and earn a spot in October with a win over the Kansas City Royals and a loss by the Rangers.
Over in the National League, the Chicago Cubs can clinch a playoff spot with a win over the Miami Marlins or a loss by the Arizona Diamondbacks. The Philadelphia Phillies can clinch a wild card if they beat the Milwaukee Brewers and either the San Diego Padres or D-backs lose.
The Padres can clinch a playoff spot with a win over the Dodgers and a loss by the D-backs.
AL Central and West are tight, other division winners are set
There's quite a bit of mediocrity in the AL Central and West divisions this season, which has led to some fascinating pennant races and could lead to a sub-.500 team making the postseason.
The Guardians (82-75) have a narrow advantage over the White Sox (81-76) in the AL Central while the Texas Rangers (78-79) and Astros (78-79) are fighting for the AL West.
Over in the National League, the playoff bracket is close to set.
The Cubs (87-70), Padres (87-70) and Phillies (87-70) are jockeying for position in the wild-card race but will almost certainly make the postseason. The only team within shouting distance is Arizona (83-74), which is four games back. Chicago holds the head-to-head tiebreaker for home field over Philadelphia and San Diego, and the Phillies own the tiebreaker over the Padres after sweeping that season series 6-0.
MLB's major awards probably won't have much drama this season.
Both MVP races have strong favorites with Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong running away with the NL honor while Houston's Yordan Alvarez is the probable choice in the AL, though Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero has also had a fantastic season. Alvarez still has an outside shot at a Triple Crown. He leads the AL in batting average at .314 and his 41 homers are tied with Caminero, but his 102 RBIs are six back of Baltimore's Pete Alonso.
For the Cy Young Award, Milwaukee flame thrower Jacob Misiorowski and New York ace Cam Schlittler are the favorites in the NL and AL, respectively.
The Rookie of the Year races also look set with Cincinnati's Sal Stewart and his 110-RBI season the leader in the NL and Detroit's Kevin McGonigle the favorite in the AL.
There are 12 teams that qualify for MLB's postseason, including six teams from both the AL and NL. The three division winners in each league get seeds No. 1 through No. 3, ranked by win-loss record. Then the three wild-card teams get seeds No. 4 through No. 6, also ranked by win-loss record.
The top two teams with the best record in both the AL and NL automatically advance to the Division Series. The other eight teams play in the Wild Card Series, which is a best-of-three format beginning on Tuesday, Sept. 29. In both the AL and NL, the No. 6 seed will travel to face the No. 3 seed while the No. 5 seed goes to No. 4. The higher seed hosts all three games.
The winners then advance to the best-of-five Division Series, followed by the best-of-seven League Championship Series and a best-of-seven World Series between the winners of the AL and NL.
Wild Card Series: Sept. 29-Oct. 1 (NBC/Peacock)
Division Series: Oct. 3-10 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
Championship Series: Oct. 11-20 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
World Series: Oct. 23-31 (FOX)
The Dodgers (+220) are the favorites to capture a third straight World Series title while the Brewers (+600), Yankees (+800) and Rays (+800) are viewed as the top contenders.
The Red Sox are adjusting the schedule of their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs because of a significant storm that's expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds to the Boston area.
The team said it was moving the Sunday afternoon game to Friday to create a split doubleheader. The first game is scheduled to begin at 1:05 p.m. EST. The originally scheduled 7:05 p.m. EST night game was moved up to 6:05.
The Red Sox said in a press release Wednesday that the change was made in consultation with Major League Baseball.
The Cubs are currently in a tight race for one of the NL's three wild-card spots.
There was no mention of a change to Saturday's game, which is slated for a 7:15 p.m. EST first pitch.
ABC7 Chicago contributed to this report.

item.title: [southsideshowdown.com] White Sox' Miguel Vargas might've somehow snuck his way into AL MVP finalist conversation
item.dc:creator: Noah Phalen
item.description: There’s very little doubt who the MVP of the Chicago White Sox has been in 2026. item.content:encoded:
There’s very little doubt who the MVP of the Chicago White Sox has been in 2026. After posting a .104 batting average in 42 games with the White Sox in 2024, very few people envisioned Miguel Vargas becoming the type of player he is now in just two years. In what feels like no time, Vargas has turned himself from a failed top prospect, to a serviceable starter, to one of MLB’s superstars. His incredible performance landed him a trip to Philadelphia for the All-Star game this summer, and it could soon land him a nomination for MLB’s most prestigious award: the MVP.
With just five games to play, the AL MVP award seems just about decided. Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has been the favorite for the majority of the season, and it’s easy to see why. In 153 games for Houston, Alvarez has slashed .314/.431/.601 with a 1.032 OPS and an AL-leading 41 home runs. Alvarez is one of the game’s most dangerous hitters and has had an impressive season from start to finish. His 6.5 fWAR is second in the American League, and as a primary DH, is completely driven by his offense. Above Alvarez is only Bobby Witt Jr, who continues to post impressive numbers despite a down year by his standards.
Immediately behind Alvarez is Yankees starter Cam Schlittler, the favorite for the AL Cy Young Award. Behind him is former White Sox ace Dylan Cease, who has excelled in his first year in Toronto. Next up? Miguel Vargas. His 5.2 fWAR ranks third among AL position players. While not impossible, it’s pretty rare that a pitcher ends up winning the MVP award. The Cy Young award essentially functions as the MVP for pitchers, so it’s very possible that Schlittler and Cease don’t become MVP finalists. That could leave Vargas next up on the list.
Miguel Vargas' underlying metrics support his excellent season
FWAR isn’t the definitive stat when it comes to a player’s value, but it’s typically a pretty good summary of a player’s offensive and defensive contributions. In 155 games this season, Vargas is slashing .251/.363/.481 with an OPS of .844 and 33 home runs, more than doubling his career high of 16 set in 2025. He’s also turned himself into a genuine threat on the bases, and his 20 steals leads the team. Vargas has elite totals in his xwOBA, xSLG, Barrel%, Sweet-Spot %, and has elite chase and walk rates, giving every indication that his breakout is real and not simply a run of good luck. If there’s any area he needs to improve, it’s his defense, but Vargas has been one of the best hitters in the American League this season.
Should Vargas be a finalist for the MVP Award, I wouldn’t expect him to win it. I wouldn’t even necessarily expect him to finish second. Alvarez is the overwhelming favorite to win the award, and Rays third-baseman Junior Caminero is the best player on the AL’s best team, giving him an edge as well. But the fact that Vargas may even be among the leaders is remarkable given the state of his career just two years ago.
Miguel Vargas isn’t just the best player on the White Sox and a building block of what they believe is an excellent young core, he’s the type of player and leader that can be the face of a franchise for many years to come. Hopefully, the writers recognize him as the backbone of MLB’s most remarkable story and reward him accordingly.

item.dc:creator: Kevin Henry

item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE — Wednesday afternoon's game between the Toronto Blue Jays and Baltimore Orioles at Oriole Park at Camden Yards had more of a spring training environment than two teams battling to stay alive in the American League postseason race deserved.
A postponement of Tuesday night's clash between the AL East rivals forced a split doubleheader on Wednesday, and the sparse crowd of 10,562 in Baltimore reflected the reality of a Wednesday matinee.
However, those in attendance were treated to more history from Pete Alonso in what has been a magical season in Charm City.
Alonso smashed a two-run homer, his 41st of the season, to pace Baltimore to a 4-2 win and stay alive for the postseason. His home run off Toronto's Max Scherzer pushed Alonso into a tie for first in the AL with Houston's Yordan Alvarez and Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero. He also ended the afternoon as the AL's leader in RBI with 110.
Pete Alonso extends the @Orioles lead with a 2-run shot ❄️ pic.twitter.com/4gBdpOtdDu
— MLB (@MLB) September 23, 2026
All of those stats and all of the things that Alonso has meant to the Orioles this season makes the veteran first baseman a strong candidate for the AL Most Valuable Player Award, said teammate Chris Bassitt.
"Pete deserves MVP votes, and he deserves them every single year. That's just the reality," Bassitt said after earning his ninth victory of the season on Wednesday afternoon. "He's one of the most underappreciated players in our game. He's easily in the top three hitters every single year."
Each of Alonso's last six hits have been home runs, becoming the first Oriole to accomplish that since Mark Trumbo hit seven home runs between Aug. 11-22, 2016.
"He's not having a crazy historical year for his standards. It's just Pete being Pete," Bassitt said. "I think Pete has held the standard of what he's done for years, and I think people are not only realizing 'Holy s--t, this guy's really good' but that he's always been really, really good."
Just how good has Alonso been? The power numbers tell the story.
Most home runs in first 8 MLB seasons:
Ralph Kiner: 329
Albert Pujols: 319
Pete Alonso: 305 https://t.co/5eKyUxKvUJ
While Alonso's blast in Wednesday afternoon's win kept the Orioles mathematically alive for the postseason, Orioles manager Craig Albernaz wanted to make sure Bassitt's 90-pitch performance wasn't overlooked.
"It was definitely a gritty outing," Albernaz said of Bassitt scattering seven hits over 5.0-plus innings but allowing just two runs. "He made pitches when he had to. He had more in the tank but he did his job today. He gave us a chance to win and threw a lot of strikes."

item.title: [MLB.com] Alonso crushes 41st homer, 1st off Scherzer as Orioles stave off elimination vs. Blue Jays

Alonso belted his 41st home run of the season to lift the Orioles to a 4-2 victory over the Blue Jays in Game 1 of a split doubleheader. item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE -- After being named the unanimous winner of the 2026 Most Valuable Oriole Award on Wednesday morning, Pete Alonso took the field at Camden Yards and continued what is shaping up to be an incredible finish to his first year in Baltimore.
Alonso belted his 41st home run of the season to lift the Orioles to a 4-2 victory over the Blue Jays in Game 1 of a split doubleheader. It marked the Polar Bear’s third homer over the first two games of this American League East rivalry series, as he swatted a pair in Monday night’s 4-3 comeback win.
It also helped the O’s stay alive in the AL Wild Card race for at least a bit longer. With an elimination number of one, Baltimore would be eliminated with either a loss in Game 2 of the twin bill against Toronto or via a White Sox win at Kansas City.
Although the Orioles may not end up in the playoffs, they continue to feel great about what Alonso has brought to the club -- and what the 31-year-old slugger should bring throughout the remainder of the five-year, $155 million contract he signed this past December.
Alonso is one of only eight players to hit 41 or more homers in a season in O’s history (since 1954), posting the ninth such campaign overall. His AL-high 110 RBIs are the most by a Baltimore player since Chris Davis had 117 in 2015.
The only AL players with as many homers as Alonso this season are Houston’s Yordan Alvarez and Tampa Bay’s Junior Caminero, who each entered Wednesday with 41.
With nine home runs over his past 18 games (and 18 homers in 41 games since Aug. 9), Alonso is continuing to climb the Orioles’ all-time single-season home run leaderboard. Next on the list is Rafael Palmeiro, who hit 43 in 1998.
Alonso, who has started every game this season, has four more games to add to his homer total -- Wednesday’s nightcap vs. the Blue Jays, followed by a three-game set against the Yankees in New York this weekend.
Despite the large contract and even larger expectations, Alonso said he hasn’t felt any added pressure to perform in 2026.
“It’s not trying to be anything different or anything more or less than who I am and what I can bring on a day-to-day basis,” Alonso said. “There’s a lot of comfort and peace of mind in that, where it’s like, ‘Hey, we believe in you, not just from a player’s side, but what you bring as a personality and teammate.’ For me, that speaks volumes.
“For me, it’s just justification. It’s like, ‘Hey, who you are, we need that, and we appreciate what you do.’ And they’re just like, ‘Go be yourself.’ What that entails is just being the best you can on the field between the lines and the best teammate you can be every single day. I really appreciate the runway, obviously.”
All season, Alonso’s leadership has drawn as much praise as his on-field performance.
“The biggest thing that stands out with Pete is, yeah, he’s going out there and competing, he wants to go out there and produce for the team, but he also wants everyone around him to do the same thing,” manager Craig Albernaz said. “He wants to help. He wants to pull everyone in the right direction, for the team and to win games.”
Alonso’s two-run blast in the fifth inning in Wednesday’s opener was his first off veteran right-hander Max Scherzer, his Mets teammate during the 2022 and ‘23 seasons. Alonso was previously 4-for-25 (.160) with two doubles, one walk and 12 strikeouts lifetime vs. Scherzer.
Right-hander Chris Bassitt turned in another solid outing, allowing two earned runs over five-plus innings. Although the 37-year-old had a 4.59 ERA in 20 games (18 starts), he recorded a 3.74 ERA over his final eight outings after returning from a back injury in mid-August.
Bassitt, who was also teammates with Alonso in New York in 2022, hasn’t been surprised at all by Alonso’s performance this season.
“Pete deserves MVP votes, and he deserves them every single year. That’s just the reality. He’s one of the most underappreciated players in our game. He’s easily a top three hitter every single year,” Bassitt said. “He’s not having a crazy historical year for his standards. It’s just Pete being Pete, and people are like, ‘Dang, this is really, really special.’ But he’s been doing that for years.
“Pete just held the standard of what he’s done for years, and I think people are now realizing, ‘Holy [crap], this guy’s really good.’ But he’s always been really, really good. So yeah, it’s Pete being Pete.”

item.content:encoded:
Yordan Alvarez, Jacob Misiorowski, AL, NL Stat Leaders Ahead of 2026 MLB Season's Final Weekend
With five days remaining in the 2026 MLB regular season, the individual stats leaderboard is almost as unsettled as the playoff races in both leagues.
The key races going into the final weekend involve Yordan Alvarez's quest for the AL triple crown and Jacob Misiorowski looking to lead all of MLB in strikeouts.
Here are the leaders in several individual categories going into Wednesday's games.
TOP NEWS
Teams Scouting Cespedes' Son 🤯
Ranking MLB's 10 Greatest Postseason Runs Since 2000 🏆
Rays' Revamped Throwback Uni 🔥
| Category | American League | National League |
| Batting Average | Yordan Alvarez (Astros): .314 | Luis Arraez (Phillies): .314 |
| Home Runs | Alvarez (Astros) and Junior Caminero (Rays): 41 | Kyle Schwarber (Phillies) and Pete Crow-Armstrong (Cubs): 45 |
| RBI | Pete Alonso (Orioles): 108 | Alec Burleson (Cardinals): 111 |
| Hits | Yandy Diaz (Rays): 175 | Otto Lopez (Marlins): 186 |
| Stolen Bases | Chandler Simpson (Rays): 46 | Nasim Nunez (Nationals): 47 |
| Wins | Sonny Gray (Red Sox): 17 | Cristopher Sánchez (Phillies): 18 |
| Innings | Michael Wacha (Royals): 194.1 | Sandy Alcantara (Marlins): 212.0 |
| ERA | Cam Schlittler (Yankees): 1.94 | Jacob Misiorowski (Brewers): 1.86 |
| Strikeouts | Gavin Williams (Guardians): 244 | Jacob Misiorowski (Brewers): 247 |
| Saves | Bryan Baker (Rays) and Cade Smith (Guardians): 40 | Riley O'Brien (Cardinals): 38 |
Alvarez will need a strong close to the season to win the triple crown. He still leads the AL in average and is tied for the lead in homers, but his RBI pace has fallen off this month.
The Houston Astros star had just five RBI in his first 16 games in September before driving in three on Tuesday in a 7-0 win over the Seattle Mariners.
Alvarez is up to 102 RBI for the season. Pete Alonso's 17 RBI this month have pushed him up to 108 with five games remaining.
Alvarez and Luis Arraez are tied for the MLB lead with a .314 batting average. Both players look like safe bets to maintain that position through Sunday.
Misiorowski, the biggest breakout star of the season for the 2026 NL Central champion Milwaukee Brewers, is looking to become the first pitcher to lead MLB in both ERA and strikeouts in a 162-game season since Jake Peavy in 2007.
The MLB ERA title is down to Misiorowski at 1.86 and New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler at 1.94. Misiorowski will likely get one more abbreviated start in Milwaukee's final regular-season series against the St. Louis Cardinals.
Schlittler is scheduled to make his final regular-season start on Thursday against the Tampa Bay Rays. Since the Yankees are locked into the No. 4 seed, he is also likely to have a shortened outing to prepare for Game 1 of the wild-card round on Tuesday.
The strikeout race is arguably more compelling than the ERA title because Gavin Williams of the Cleveland Guardians will likely get the nod on Friday against the Kansas City Royals.
Since the Guardians can't wrap up the AL Central until Friday at the earliest, Williams will likely have a regular outing. He is currently only three Ks behind Misiorowski for the MLB lead.
Williams has 15 strikeouts in 11.2 innings against the Royals this season, but he hasn't faced them since May 5.
NL MVP favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong is one stolen base away from the seventh player in MLB history to have a 40-40 season. He can also become the first Chicago Cubs player to lead the NL in homers since Sammy Sosa hit 49 in 2002.

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Astros’ Yordan Alvarez joins Albert Pujols, Barry Bonds in MLB history
item.dc:creator: Chris Trant
item.description: The Houston Astros have endured an unusually inconsistent 2026 MLB season, but remain firmly in playoff contention as the final week of the regular season continues. Houston enters Wednesday’s matchup with the Seattle Mariners at 78-79, tied for first place in the American League West with the Texas Rangers. Although the Astros have lost seven of their last ten games and remain below .500, they still find themselves fighting for a division title with just five games to go. No player has done mor
item.content:encoded:
The Houston Astros have endured an unusually inconsistent 2026 MLB season, but remain firmly in playoff contention as the final week of the regular season continues.
Houston enters Wednesday’s matchup with the Seattle Mariners at 78-79, tied for first place in the American League West with the Texas Rangers. Although the Astros have lost seven of their last ten games and remain below .500, they still find themselves fighting for a division title with just five games to go.
No player has done more to keep the Astros in the playoff race than Yordan Alvarez. After a 2025 season that was plagued by injuries, Alvarez has bounced back in 2026, putting together the best regular season of his career.
A Career Year in Houston
The four-time All-Star is slashing .314/.431/.601, adding 41 home runs and 102 RBIs through 153 games. His 1.033 OPS is the best in baseball this season, and he is tied with Junior Caminero for the most home runs in the American League.
Alvarez has continued to come through while the Astros fight for the division lead. Tuesday against the Mariners, he homered and drove in three runs in a 7-0 victory that helped the Astros pull back into a tie in the division with the Rangers.
For Alvarez, his combination of production, power, and respect from opposing managers has placed him in rare historical company.
Baseball Royalty
According to Francys Romero, Alvarez is “now just the 5th player in MLB with 40+ HR, 100+ RBI and 30+ intentional walks in a single season before turning 30.”
The only other players to accomplish the feat are Albert Pujols, Ryan Howard, Barry Bonds and Kevin Mitchell. Pujols was the most recent, doing so during the 2009 season with the St. Louis Cardinals.
Joining this elite company shines a light on just how dominant Alvarez’s season has been, and how crucial he has been in keeping the team’s season alive.
Still fighting for the AL West crown, the Astros will need Alvarez to maintain his MVP-caliber production if the team hopes to secure a postseason spot and make a run in October.

item.content:encoded:
By LUKE OLSON Associated Press
SEATTLE (AP) — Yordan Alvarez resumed his Triple Crown push with a home run and three RBIs as the Houston Astros beat the Seattle Mariners 7-0 on Tuesday night to pull even with Texas atop the AL West.
Houston snapped a three-game skid and tied the Rangers at 78-79 following their 6-3 loss to the New York Mets at home. Both teams have five games remaining, and the Astros hold the head-to-head tiebreaker.
Seattle (73-84) is on the brink of playoff elimination, one season after winning the AL West for the first time in 24 years and coming within one victory of the franchise’s first World Series appearance.
Alvarez hit a two-run drive to right field in the eighth inning to tie Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays for the American League lead with 41 homers. Alvarez is first in batting average at .314 and he has 102 RBIs, six behind Baltimore Orioles slugger Pete Alonso for most in the AL.
Miguel Cabrera of the Detroit Tigers in 2012 was the most recent hitter to win a Triple Crown by leading his league in all three of those statistical categories.
Alvarez hit an RBI single in the first to reach 100 RBIs for the second time in his career. Christian Walker belted a three-run homer to make it 4-0 in the third, and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot in the sixth.
It was the 200th home run of Walker’s career and his 26th this season.
Cam Smith snapped an 0-for-26 skid with a double.
Houston starter Cristian Javier was removed after two innings with right groin tightness. He threw 45 pitches. Miguel Ullola (1-0) followed with two innings of one-hit ball for his first major league win.
Bennett Sousa, AJ Blubaugh and Logan VanWey completed the four-hitter.
Mariners starter Logan Gilbert (12-11) lasted only four innings, yielding four runs on 10 hits — the most hits he’s allowed in a game this season.
Up next
Rookie right-hander Ethan Pecko (1-0, 3.77 ERA) makes his fifth major league start Wednesday for Houston against Seattle RHP George Kirby (9-11, 4.24).
___
This story has been corrected to show that Alvarez homered in the eighth inning.
___

item.title: [FanSided] The stats make Mets' Pete Alonso decision look historically bad
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman

item.content:encoded:
Pete Alonso has spent much of the last week going viral, much to Baltimore Orioles fans’ pleasure and New York Mets fans’ … well, we’d call it dismay, but Citi Field viewed things far differently.
Alonso has since left New York in more ways than one, and the Orioles are back in Charm City for their final home series. The five-time All-Star hit his 39th and 40th homers in Monday’s 4-3 win over the Blue Jays, becoming only the ninth player in franchise history to join such a club.
Fans might dig the long ball, but Alonso has done far more than round the bases so frequently. He entered Tuesday leading the American League with 108 RBIs, and he's only three behind the Cardinals' Alec Burleson for the most in the majors. Despite a relatively slow start, the veteran first baseman has a healthy lead over the Astros' Yordan Alvarez (99) and Rays' Junior Caminero (97) with six games left.
All of that sounds great, but here’s the kicker: At his current pace, Alonso would become the first player in MLB history to lead the AL and NL in RBIs in two separate seasons; he and Aaron Judge tied for an MLB-high 131 RBIs in 2022.
Pete Alonso continues to further humiliate Steve Cohen’s New York Mets
First off, can we just appreciate the fact that no player has ever won the RBI title in separate leagues? You’d think Frank Robinson would have done it seeing as he became the first player to win the MVP in both the AL and NL, but apparently not. Our dark horse pick would have been Mark McGwire.
Alonso’s 4.6 bWAR is his highest since 2019, and he's on track to finish with career highs in on-base percentage (.359) and walk rate (11.4 percent). He cleared the 300-homer mark last week and is currently at 304, so he stands an excellent chance at reaching 400 within the coming years.
All of this follows the Mets allegedly not making Alonso — their all-time home run leader and one of the most beloved players in the post-David Wright era — a formal contract offer this past offseason. Steve Cohen and David Stearns instead opted for Jorge Polanco, who hit .148 with a .431 OPS and -1.4 bWAR over 37 games. Great job, all.
The concerns about how Alonso would age as a power-heavy first baseman were valid, but not offering him a contract easily ranks among the worst decisions in Mets history. You don’t let one of your all-time greats leave without a fight, especially not when he’s still playing at an All-Star level. It’s not like Alonso had a realistic chance to receive $300 million on the open market.
But “what could have been” is the story of the New York Mets’ existence. How far would they have gone in the postseason had they not collapsed in 2007, 2008, and 2025? Would Tom Seaver have helped the Mets return to form rather than join the Reds in the “Midnight Massacre?”
At least Alonso seemingly landed in a place where leadership respects him — and if they’re smart, they’ll consult him on any potential offseason moves. Here’s an idea: Do everything that the Mets wouldn’t do.

item.title: [heraldglobe.com] MLB roundup: Drew Rasmussen helps Rays smother Yankees for AL East title
item.description:
Field Level Media
23 Sep 2026, 12:25 GMT+10
(Photo credit: Brad Penner) Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the American League East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader. The Rays won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games. Yandy
item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 12:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the American League East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader.
The Rays won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games. Yandy Diaz drove in four runs on a pair of singles.
Rasmussen (16-5) took a no-hitter into the seventh until Heliot Ramos opened the inning with a double to left for New York. Ramos eventually scored on an RBI single by rookie George Lombard Jr. off Kevin Kelly.
Rasmussen finished with 11 strikeouts for his fourth career double-digit strikeout performance. He finished two shy of his career-high set June 10 against the Boston Red Sox and the Rays won his 12th consecutive start.
Yankees 2, Rays 0 (Game 1)
Cody Bellinger hit a two-run home run in the fourth inning as host New York recorded a shutout over Tampa Bay in the opener of a day-night doubleheader.
With the victory, the Yankees temporarily prevented the Rays from clinching the AL East and moved six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox for the American League's top wild-card spot.
New York's Carlos Rodon (7-3) scattered three singles over eight innings as the Yankees finished off the victory in a brisk 2 hours, 2 minutes. Rodon struck out eight in his 100th career win and also reached 1,500 strikeouts for his career. Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-5) allowed two runs on five hits over six innings with seven strikeouts to take his first loss since July 9.
Dodgers 7, Padres 0
Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs, and Los Angeles inched closer to the best record in the National League with a shutout of visiting San Diego.
Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games.
Los Angeles moved to within one game of the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the National League Division Series to one. Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two.
Phillies 6, Brewers 4
Bryson Stott delivered the tiebreaking hit in the eighth inning to guide Philadelphia to a victory over visiting Milwaukee. Brandon Marsh homered and knocked in three runs as the Phillies lowered their magic number to two to clinch a postseason berth.
Zack Wheeler ended up with a no-decision after striking out 11 while giving up three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings. Wheeler struck out the first seven batters he faced, setting a Phillies record for consecutive strikeouts to begin a game. His first-inning strikeout of Brice Turang was the 2,000th of his career.
The Brewers saw their lead over the Dodgers for the top record in the majors shrink to one as they lost just the third time in their last 13 games. William Contreras knocked in three runs.
Marlins 8, Cubs 2 (12 innings)
Griffin Conine plated the go-ahead run that ignited a six-run 12th inning for visiting Miami, which snapped a three-game losing by beating Chicago and postponing the Cubs' playoff celebration for at least a day.
On a night when runs were scarce until the final inning, both teams endured a pair of scoreless extra frames before Conine broke the drought with a leadoff, golf-shot single off Caleb Thielbar that fell just inside the left field line. Esteury Ruiz, the automatic runner, scored from second to make it 3-2 as the Marlins sent 10 batters to the plate in the inning.
The Cubs could have clinched a wild-card playoff spot with a win or Arizona loss, but neither of those happened keeping the Diamondbacks mathematically alive. Josh Ekness (3-4) struck out a pair in the 11th inning to get the win while Thielbar (3-4) gave up three runs -- two earned -- in his inning of work.
Guardians 3, Red Sox 2
Nathaniel Lowe drove in Chase DeLauter with a sacrifice fly in the ninth inning and Cleveland held on to beat host Boston in the first game of a three-game series.
Cleveland not only extended its winning streak to six but maintained its one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox for first place in the AL Central.
Parker Messick held Boston to one run on five hits in five innings, his 14th straight start allowing three runs or fewer. Payton Tolle started for the Red Sox and gave up two runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings as the Guardians went 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position and stranded 15.
White Sox 14, Royals 11
Chase Meidroth smacked a three-run home run among his three hits and drove in five, and Brenton Doyle, Randal Grichuk and Munetaka Murakami also homered to power Chicago past host Kansas City.
Chicago won for the fourth time in five games to remain one game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians. The White Sox, who hold the third and final AL wild-card spot, reduced their magic number to earn a playoff berth to three.
Vinnie Pasquantino hit a ninth-inning grand slam for the Royals, who lost their fifth straight. He went 3-for-5 with a double and also drove in five.
Nationals 3, Tigers 1
CJ Abrams hit a pair of home runs and drove in all three runs as visiting Washington topped Detroit. Abrams reached 100 RBIs for the season with his solo shot in the second inning, then broke a 1-1 tie in the seventh with his 33rd long ball of the season, a two-run blast.
Dylan Crews had two hits and scored the other run for the Nationals. Rookie Jackson Kent (2-4) earned the win in long relief. He allowed one run on six hits over four innings and struck out three. Opener Riley Cornelio lasted 2 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking three.
Ben Malgeri scored the Tigers' only run. Kevin McGonigle and Max Clark each had two hits.
Pirates 2, Cardinals 0
Jared Jones and two relievers combined on a one-hitter as Pittsburgh beat visiting St. Louis for a fifth straight win. Jones (5-6) lowered his ERA to 1.08 in four September starts and struck out nine with zero walks over seven innings while throwing 63 of his 86 pitches for strikes.
Pittsburgh broke a scoreless tie with two outs in the sixth inning on Ryan O'Hearn's RBI single against Andre Pallante (12-8). Pallante allowed one run on three hits with two walks and two strikeouts over six innings.
St. Louis struck out 14 times and lost for the fifth time in its last six games.
Astros 7, Mariners 0
Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as Houston slugged and pitched its way past host Seattle.
Jose Altuve, Yainer Diaz, Alvarez and Paredes each collected two hits for the Astros, who pulled into a first-place tie with the Texas Rangers in the West. Five Astros pitchers combined to throw a four-hit shutout. Miguel Ullola (1-0) earned his first major league win, allowing one hit and striking out two over two innings of relief.
Julio Rodriguez notched two hits for Seattle. The Mariners went 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine.
Reds 4, Braves 0
Brandon Williamson fired six scoreless innings and Cincinnati supported him with three solo homers to defeat host Atlanta in the opener of a three-game series.
Cincinnati ended a two-game losing streak and evened the season series with Atlanta at 2-2. Williamson (5-4) worked six scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two strikeouts. Elly De La Cruz (29), Dane Myers (8) and Eugenio Suarez (25) each hit a home run for the Reds. It was Suarez's 350th career homer, making him the 10th active player to reach that mark.
Atlanta starter JR Ritchie (1-4) pitched five innings and allowed one run on four hits and three walks. The rookie struck out a career-high eight batters.
Mets 6, Rangers 3
Francisco Alvarez laced a go-ahead two-run double in the sixth, then scored an insurance run on an unusual sacrifice fly for visiting New York, who damaged Texas' playoff hopes with a win in the opener of a three-game interleague series in Arlington.
Juan Soto had an RBI single in the third, and Carson Benge capped the scoring with a run-scoring double in the seventh for the Mets. The club won hours after removing the interim tag from manager Andy Green and signing him to a three-year extension.
Josh Jung had an RBI double in the third, and Elias Diaz and Wyatt Langford lofted sacrifice flies in the fourth for the Rangers, who entered Tuesday with a one-game lead over the Houston Astros in the AL West.
Diamondbacks 7, Rockies 2
Nolan Arenado homered and doubled among his three hits, Michael Soroka tossed seven strong innings, and Arizona kept its slim postseason hopes alive with a win over host Colorado in Denver.
Geraldo Perdomo also had three hits and Ildemaro Vargas finished with two hits for Arizona, which remains alive in the NL wild-card race, sitting four games behind Philadelphia, San Diego and the Chicago Cubs for the third and final spot with five games to go.
Mickey Moniak homered for Colorado, which finished with just three hits and just one after the third inning. The Rockies (57-100) are the first team to lose 100 or more games in four straight seasons since the 1962-65 New York Mets.
Twins 3, Giants 2
Walker Jenkins homered, Luke Keaschall contributed both offensively and defensively, and Minnesota evened its road interleague series against San Francisco.
Taj Bradley (12-6) combined with four relievers on a six-hitter for the Twins, who used two late diving catches by Keaschall in right field to prevent the Giants from taking the first two of the series.
Bradley allowed just one other hit -- a fifth-inning single by Drew Gilbert -- in his six innings. He walked three and struck out six. Keaschall's one-out triple scored Ryan Kreidler, then Brooks Lee gave Minnesota the lead for good with a run-scoring single to plate Keaschall.
A's 9, Angels 7
Carlos Cortes hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the bottom of the eighth inning and the Athletics overcame a six-run deficit to beat Los Angeles in West Sacramento, Calif.
In addition to the homer off Sam Bachman, Cortes also delivered a pinch-hit RBI triple in the seventh, helping the Athletics end a six-game losing streak. Zack Gelof hit a two-run homer later in the eighth for the A's. Shea Langeliers and Lawrence Butler each had three hits and an RBI for the Athletics.
Denzer Guzman homered and drove in four RBIs for the Angels, who have lost four of their last six games. Mike Trout added three hits and two runs for Los Angeles (60-97), which has never lost 100 games in a season.
Blue Jays at Orioles, ppd.
The scheduled game between Toronto and host Baltimore was postponed due to ongoing inclement weather. The game will be made up as part of a split doubleheader on Wednesday, with games starting at 1:35 p.m. and 6:35 p.m. ET.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 10:35 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Joe Nicholson)
Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as the visiting Houston Astros slugged their way to a 7-0 victory over the Seattle Mariners on Tuesday.
Jose Altuve, Yainer Diaz, Alvarez and Paredes each collected two hits for the Astros (78-79), who pulled into a first-place tie with the Texas Rangers in the American League West. Houston owns the head-to-head tiebreaker over Texas, so would win the division if the teams remain tied at the end of the season.
Five Astros pitchers combined to throw a four-hit shutout. Miguel Ullola (1-0) earned his first major league win, allowing one hit and striking out two over two innings.
Julio Rodriguez notched two hits for Seattle (73-84). The Mariners went 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine.
Jeremy Pena led off the game with an infield single to shortstop, stole second, and scored on Alvarez's single to right. It marked the 100th RBI of the season for Alvarez, the second time in his career he's reached that milestone. Paredes and Altuve followed with singles, loading the bases with no outs.
Seattle starter Logan Gilbert (12-11) escaped the first-inning jam when Diaz struck out looking before Walker and Taylor Trammell flied out.
Altuve and Diaz opened the third with back-to-back singles before Walker launched his 26th home run of the season and the 200th of his career, a three-run shot to deep left, giving the Astros a 4-0 lead.
In the fifth, J.P. Crawford drew a one-out walk. After Randy Arozarena struck out swinging, Dominic Canzone singled to center. Crawford advanced to third, but Cal Raleigh struck out to end the inning.
Houston's advantage increased to 5-0 on Paredes' solo homer in the sixth.
With one out in the eighth, Pena was hit by a pitch, and Alvarez belted a slider over the wall in right for his 41st home run of the season, extending Houston's lead to 7-0.
Houston starter Cristian Javier tossed two shutout innings, allowing one hit and two walks while striking out two. The Astros announced Javier exited the game with groin tightness.
Gilbert gave up four runs on 10 hits over four innings, walking two and striking out three.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [Bozeman Daily Chronicle] Triple Crown still within reach for Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez after big game in Seattle
item.dc:creator: LUKE OLSON
item.description: SEATTLE (AP) — Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez gained some ground Tuesday night in his chase for a Triple Crown. He still has plenty of work to do this week. item.content:encoded:
SEATTLE (AP) — Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez gained some ground Tuesday night in his chase for a Triple Crown.
He still has plenty of work to do this week.
The AL MVP front-runner went 2 for 4 with his 41st home run and three RBIs in the Astros' 7-0 win over the Seattle Mariners. Alvarez hit an RBI single in the first inning, was intentionally walked in the second and then belted a 386-foot homer in the eighth with a 109.5 mph exit velocity.
“At this point, I keep wondering why guys are pitching to him,” Houston first baseman Christian Walker said. “He just seems to come through in every moment. He's dangerous at the plate right now.”
Alvarez, who is quiet and shows little emotion, orchestrated a team meeting after the Astros (78-79) were swept by Atlanta on Sunday, squandering their lead in the AL West. His performance on Tuesday was much-needed to put Houston in a tie with the Texas Rangers atop the division with five games left this season.
“He's been backing it up all year,” Astros manager Joe Espada said.
Alvarez's two-run shot to right field tied him with Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays for the American League lead with 41 homers. Alvarez is first in batting average at .314 — five points ahead of Tampa Bay's Chandler Simpson — and he has 102 RBIs, six behind Baltimore Orioles slugger Pete Alonso for most in the AL.
Alonso drove in three runs with two homers Monday against Toronto, but the teams were rained out Tuesday in Baltimore because of bad weather. They are scheduled to play a split doubleheader Wednesday.
Alvarez has six homers since Aug. 1, and the 29-year-old designated hitter has eight RBIs over 17 games in September. He'll need more to become baseball’s first Triple Crown winner since Miguel Cabrera in 2012.
Alvarez leads the AL in slugging percentage (.601), OPS (1.032), total bases (329) and walks (106). Logan Gilbert intentionally walked Alvarez in the second inning Tuesday, which was the 33rd time for Alvarez this season, already a franchise record.
It’s been a historic season for the four-time All-Star after he was limited to 48 games in 2025 because of a broken hand and an ankle injury.
If he wins the AL MVP award, the Cuban slugger will join Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers as the only players to win an MVP award while primarily serving as a designated hitter. Othani was close to winning a Triple Crown in 2024 after leading the NL in homers (50) and RBIs (130), but his .310 average fell just short to Luis Arráez’s .314.

Yordan Alvarez went 2-for-4 with a home run, three RBI, and a walk to lead the Astros to a 7-0 win over the Mariners on Tuesday.

item.title: [Claro Sports] Pete Alonso busca una marca histórica que nadie ha conseguido en 106 años de Grandes Ligas
item.dc:creator: Juan Carlos Campos Rodríguez
item.description: El primera base de los Orioles está cerca de alcanzar un registro que no tiene registro desde hace más de un siglo en las Grandes Ligas Pete Alonso está cerca de conseguir una marca inédita en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El Oso Polar vive una temp
item.content:encoded:
El primera base de los Orioles está cerca de alcanzar un registro que no tiene registro desde hace más de un siglo en las Grandes Ligas
Pete Alonso está cerca de conseguir una marca inédita en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. El primera base de los Orioles de Baltimore tiene la oportunidad de convertirse en el primer jugador en más de un siglo de MLB que termina como líder de carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas, una estadística oficial que se tiene registro desde 1920.
El Oso Polar vive una temporada destacada con Baltimore y llega a la recta final del calendario como uno de los principales productores ofensivos de la Liga Americana. Su objetivo es completar una hazaña que ningún pelotero ha logrado desde la creación de las Grandes Ligas modernas.
La posibilidad de Alonso tiene como antecedente su rendimiento cuando formaba parte de la Liga Nacional. El toletero ya consiguió encabezar ese departamento en 2022 con los Mets de Nueva York y ahora busca repetir la hazaña del otro lado de la MLB con los Mets de Nueva York.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Justin Verlander prepara su última apertura en las Grandes Ligas
Alonso busca dominar las carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas
El reto de Pete Alonso está relacionado con su capacidad para producir carreras, una de las principales características que ha mostrado durante su trayectoria en las Grandes Ligas.
El primera base llegó a la temporada 2026 con una carrera consolidada como uno de los bateadores de mayor poder en MLB y ahora tiene la oportunidad de sumar un logro que ningún jugador ha alcanzado en 106 años de historia.
Durante su etapa anterior en la Liga Nacional, Alonso logró posicionarse como uno de los mejores productores ofensivos del circuito con 131 carreras impulsadas. Ahora, con los Orioles, busca repetir ese dominio en la Liga Americana.
De acuerdo con los registros históricos, ningún pelotero ha terminado una temporada como líder de carreras impulsadas en ambas ligas, por lo que Alonso podría convertirse en el primero en conseguirlo.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Alex Bregman recibe pelotazo en el rostro y abandona juego
Una temporada histórica con los Orioles
Pete Alonso llegó a Baltimore como una de las principales incorporaciones ofensivas del equipo y rápidamente asumió un papel importante dentro del orden al bate. El jugador ha mantenido su capacidad para generar extrabases y producir carreras, características que lo han acompañado desde su debut en MLB en 2019.
Además de su producción ofensiva, Alonso continúa ampliando su legado dentro del béisbol profesional. En 2026 también alcanzó una marca importante al llegar a los 300 cuadrangulares en su carrera, logro que consiguió como jugador de los Orioles frente a los Mets, su antiguo equipo.
Alonso busca entrar en la historia de MLB
La recta final de la temporada será determinante para conocer si Pete Alonso consigue completar una de las hazañas más difíciles del béisbol moderno. A menos de una semana de finalizar su primera temporada con los Orioles de Baltimore, Pete Alonso se mantiene en la pelea por una marca histórica. El primera base suma 108 carreras impulsadas, nueve más que el cubano Yordan Álvarez, quien acumula 99 y ocupa el segundo lugar de la Liga Americana en este departamento.
Con la recta final del calendario por disputarse, Alonso tiene una ventaja importante para quedarse con el liderato de impulsadas. Salvo que Álvarez tenga una última semana extraordinaria, el jugador de Baltimore podría terminar la campaña en la cima de este rubro y acercarse a una hazaña que no se consigue desde hace más de un siglo.

item.title: [blogs.fangraphs.com] Yankees Face Judge Dread
item.dc:creator: Michael Baumann
item.description: When Aaron Judge is healthy, he’s the most dangerous hitter in baseball. Sometimes I get alarmed at how uncontroversial a statement that is; ours is a sport that so frequently humiliates those who make such sweeping, unequivocal judgments as those. But the empirical evidence is what it is. Judge has played 150 or more games in a season four times in his career. item.content:encoded:
When Aaron Judge is healthy, he’s the most dangerous hitter in baseball. Sometimes I get alarmed at how uncontroversial a statement that is; ours is a sport that so frequently humiliates those who make such sweeping, unequivocal judgments as those.
But the empirical evidence is what it is. Judge has played 150 or more games in a season four times in his career. In those four seasons, he’s led all position players in WAR four times and led the league in wRC+ three times. He’s been named AL MVP three times and finished second once, ahead of some real doozies: Cal Raleigh’s 60-homer year, Bobby Witt Jr.’s 10.5-WAR campaign in 2024, Shohei Ohtani’s best pitching season — in fact, a healthy Judge is the only thing that’s ever trumped a healthy Ohtani in an MVP race.
So again, it’s not uncontroversial to say that when Judge is healthy he’s the best hitter in the world. He has not, however, always been healthy. Least of all this season, when he missed three months with a broken rib. And now, the single-season AL home run king is back on the IL with a calf strain. The timing could not be worse.
Judge last played on Wednesday, leaving open the option to activate him on Sunday for the final game of the regular season. That seems like a theoretical concern at the moment rather than a practical one. Our Matt Martell was at Yankee manager Aaron Boone’s pregame media availability on Tuesday morning, where Boone illustrated the inadequacy of a return-to-play timeline at this point in the season.
“We’re planning on [Judge] not being a part of [the Wild Card Series],” Boone said. “You hear all the time with injuries, we give ranges: two to four weeks, four to six. They’re ranges for a reason. We’re at a point in the year where, obviously, we’d push it a little bit if that was in play, but that’s a week away. I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out either.”
That’s the problem. A range of two weeks in recovery time isn’t a big deal in a six-month season, but even one week is twice as long as the Yankees’ entire first playoff round. And muscle injuries can be finicky to begin with — you go to bed one night feeling fine and wake up the next morning with weakness or stiffness.
For what it’s worth, the Yankees are technically still alive in the AL East race as of this writing, but you can forgive Boone for speaking as if the division is already lost.
Either way, in order to speed things along, Judge received a platelet-poor plasma (PPP) injection on Monday, not to be confused with a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection.
Now, apparently having read The Magic School Bus Inside the Human Body as a child is not a sufficient qualification to perform surgery on live patients. At least, that’s what the police told me. But anyone who’s read that book can tell you the makeup of human blood: Red blood cells, which carry oxygen; white blood cells, which fight infection; platelets, which stop bleeding and heal wounds; and plasma, which is the broth all the other stuff floats around in.
PRP injections are a pretty common treatment for sports injuries, but taking the healing bits out of plasma seems kind of counterintuitive. Sort of like a vodka-poor screwdriver. But evidently PPP contains high levels of fibrinogen, which is itself a healing agent. Ms. Frizzle didn’t cover fibrinogen, but sure, I’ll buy it.
Unless the PPP works an actual miracle, though, it looks like the Yankees are going to have to navigate at least the first round of the playoffs without their best player.
And even if Judge does return — either in the Wild Card round or later, if the Yankees advance — I’d caution against assuming that we’d be seeing the best of him right off the proverbial bat. For starters, 99% of star athletes in history are going to try to force their way into the lineup for the playoffs regardless of whether they’re actually healthy.
To say nothing of the fact that Judge can be streaky. This is the nature of Judge’s unusual skill set; there are 1,073 hitters in major league history with at least 5,000 career plate appearances. Judge is the only one of those who’s produced one of the three true outcomes (home run, strikeout, walk) in more than half of his career plate appearances. (I’d like to express my immense gratitude to Adam Dunn, who has a career TTO% of 49.9, for making this fun fact possible.)
Living on the extremes, as he does, Judge will have weeks where he homers every night, and others where he goes 1-for-20 with 12 strikeouts. But you live with it because, over a long enough timeline, it works out heavily in his favor. Among hitters with at least 5,000 career plate appearances, Judge has the third-highest career wRC+, trailing only Babe Ruth and Ted Williams. If you wanted to go further than “best hitter now” and anoint Judge the best hitter ever, leaning heavily on the argument that quality of competition increases over time, you’d have a credible case.
But that’s not what the Yankees got out of Judge this year. In 66 regular-season games, he’s hit .241/.360/.511, with his highest strikeout rate (29.8%) since 2019 and lowest wRC+ (141) since 2020. In seven games since he returned from his rib injury, Judge was just 4-for-23 with one home run, one walk, and 13 strikeouts.
I’ve done enough of these injury reaction posts to figure out that they’re not really about the guy who got hurt, but about the teammates he’s leaving behind.
And I don’t want to underrate the value of Judge — even the version of Judge that has a 141 wRC+, rather than a 200 wRC+ — but the Yankees have done OK without him.
In the weakest American League field in decades, the Yankees are one of only two teams with a winning percentage of .550 or better. Entering their doubleheader with the Rays on Tuesday, the Yankees are still first in the AL in home runs (216) and second in runs scored per game (4.60). Even without Judge (or Giancarlo Stanton, for that matter), their lineup has plenty of beef.
| Name | G | PA | HR | BB% | K% | AVG | OBP | SLG | wOBA | xwOBA | wRC+ | WAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ben Rice | 148 | 641 | 39 | 12.6% | 23.9% | .261 | .360 | .528 | .381 | .376 | 147 | 4.0 |
| Aaron Judge | 66 | 285 | 18 | 15.1% | 29.8% | .241 | .360 | .511 | .372 | .396 | 141 | 2.0 |
| Cody Bellinger | 128 | 546 | 16 | 10.6% | 15.8% | .270 | .344 | .435 | .341 | .338 | 119 | 3.7 |
| Paul Goldschmidt | 102 | 370 | 18 | 7.8% | 23.0% | .253 | .316 | .455 | .334 | .314 | 114 | 1.7 |
| Luis García Jr. | 39 | 153 | 7 | 4.6% | 20.9% | .276 | .307 | .462 | .332 | .320 | 113 | 0.6 |

| Jazz Chisholm Jr. | 134 | 520 | 19 | 10.4% | 29.4% | .232 | .312 | .403 | .313 | .296 | 100 | 3.4 |
| Trent Grisham | 121 | 484 | 18 | 12.6% | 18.4% | .211 | .308 | .395 | .311 | .337 | 98 | 0.7 |

| George Lombard Jr. | 37 | 146 | 5 | 6.8% | 24.7% | .235 | .290 | .386 | .296 | .298 | 88 | 0.3 |

Blue: Platoon
Red: Currently or recently injured
Ben Rice in particular has been absolutely terrific this season. He’s fourth among qualified AL hitters in wRC+ and third in both home runs and runs scored. The Astros have AL MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez in their lineup; apart from him, is there any hitter in the AL bracket who’s been Rice’s equal this year? Maybe Junior Caminero? Willson Contreras, if you value OBP over raw power? Even if you’re being charitable, it’s a short list.
Now, past Rice, things get interesting, because if you want to talk about the Yankees’ offensive depth, you have to be able to hold multiple ideas in your head at once.
As of Tuesday morning, the Yankees have 11 hitters with double-digit home runs this season, which is tied for the most in the league. That’s just counting players who have hit 10 or more home runs in pinstripes, and the Yankees brought in substantial reinforcements midseason. Luis García Jr. has just seven homers for the Yankees but 30 overall. Heliot Ramos has four home runs in 32 games and 13 overall, with 20-plus in each of his previous two seasons. George Lombard Jr. has just five home runs in 37 major league games, but he hit 12 dingers in 78 minor league games before he got called up.
Count all this up and the Yankees have more hitters with at least decent pop than they can fit on the roster at once.
At the same time, Rice is the only Yankee with 20 home runs in pinstripes this year. So while this lineup is short on automatic outs, if Judge is out, there’s a massive drop-off after Rice.
If you take Judge out of the picture, Cody Bellinger is second on the Yankees in wRC+, at 119. The Rays don’t have anyone with 100 or more plate appearances and a better wRC+ than Rice this season, but they have four hitters (Caminero, Yandy Díaz, Jonathan Aranda, and Victor Mesa Jr.) with 100 or more plate appearances and a better wRC+ than Bellinger. So do the Rangers (Justin Foscue, Josh Jung, Joc Pederson, Wyatt Langford). The Astros have Alvarez, plus Isaac Paredes and Jeremy Peña. The White Sox have Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami, and Tristan Peters.
As good as Rice has been, the Yankees’ lineup looks concerningly pedestrian without Judge. If you aren’t already a FanGraphs Member, please consider becoming one; it’s the only way to get trenchant original analysis like this.
The good news is that Judge’s calf injury runs counter to the rest of the team’s injury luck. Carlos Rodón, who missed almost three months with an elbow injury earlier this year, dominated the Rays in eight scoreless innings in Game 1 of a doubleheader on Tuesday. The same day, the Yankees activated Chisholm, who’d spent two weeks on the IL with a sprained thumb. Clarke Schmidt just returned from Tommy John surgery last week, and while he suffered biceps cramping in the bullpen on Sunday, it appears to be a minor setback. Trent Grisham remains a question mark for the start of the playoffs as he recovers from a hamstring injury, but his prognosis also looks good.
Judge is as important to the Yankees as any two or three other players put together, but with a healthy and deep rotation and Rice leading the way offensively, they’re not in bad shape. The remainder of this roster could easily survive and advance through a weaker AL bracket, setting the stage for a dramatically timed Judge return in mid-October. Like Kirk Gibson, only bigger.
Michael is a writer at FanGraphs. Previously, he was a staff writer at The Ringer and D1Baseball, and his work has appeared at Grantland, Baseball Prospectus, The Atlantic, ESPN.com, and various ill-remembered Phillies blogs. Follow him on Twitter, if you must, @MichaelBaumann.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Why Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber Are Key to Phillies Playoff Success
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Teape; Unknown
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies have a little bit of work left to do to secure a playoff spot in the National League. item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies have a little bit of work left to do to secure a playoff spot in the National League.
With six games remaining in the regular season, the Phillies hold a four-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks. But because they do not possess the tiebreaker, Philadelphia still has a Magic Number of three.
Over the next six games, they need some combination of three victories of their own and losses by the Diamondbacks. They are heavily favored to make the postseason field, but then will be jostling for seeding with the Chicago Cubs, who are currently the No. 1 Wild Card team, and the San Diego Padres, who are currently No. 2.
To catch those teams and make any noise in the playoffs, the Phillies are going to need their stars to play up to their capabilities. Two players they will be counting on to produce are right fielder Bryce Harper and designated hitter Kyle Schwarber.
Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber have been elite against fastballs
In the playoffs, there is a little extra juice when facing opponents. Pitchers are throwing the ball a little harder, and handling velocity becomes a key component for a team to find success. Luckily for Philadelphia, their two star sluggers are among the best in baseball when facing heat.
Some of the nastiest offerings in baseball are off-speed and breaking pitches that can play up a four-seam fastball. So, when a batter gets the opportunity to jump one of those fastballs, they need to make it count.
Harper and Schwarber both accomplish that. As shared by David Adler of MLB.com, thus far in 2026, they are two of the most productive players in the MLB against fastballs. Schwarber is second in the MLB with a batting run value of +30 runs created, which trails only Yordan Alvarez of the Houston Astros, who has +32.
The Phillies slugger has launched 27 home runs against fastballs this season, which is the most in the MLB. Harper has hit 18 home runs when facing fastballs, and his +28 runs created is the third most in baseball. Willson Contreras of the Boston Red Sox and Ben Rice of the New York Yankees round out the top five with +25 and +23 runs created apiece.
Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber produce under brightest lights
While the Philadelphia duo has succeeded against that pitch type, they have also gotten the job done even when the pitcher is throwing with elite velocity. When facing fastballs that are 97 mph or faster this season, Harper has a slugging percentage of .523 with three long balls.
Schwarber has been slightly better, with a .525 slugging percentage and six home runs, which once again leads the MLB.
Even more encouraging for the Phillies is that since the two became teammates, their production against fastballs is even better in the playoffs. Harper has an eye-popping .778 slugging percentage with eight home runs since 2022, making him the best fastball hitter in the MLB postseason during that span.
Schwarber has 10 home runs in the playoffs with a .722 slugging percentage. Hopefully, they keep that production up to help Philadelphia advance in the postseason.

During his time at Old Westbury, he worked for the school newspaper and several online publications, such as Knicks Now, the official website of the New York Knicks, and a self-made website with fellow students, Gotham City Sports News. item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Pete Crow-Armstrong is chasing more than just an MVP
item.dc:creator: Kendall Baker

Now, in the final week of the regular season, the Cubs centerfielder is looking to put the finishing touches on one of the greatest all-around campaigns in baseball history. item.content:encoded:
Yahoo Sports AM is our daily newsletter that keeps you up to date on all things sports. Sign up here to get it every weekday morning.
⚾️ Forget MVP. PCA is chasing history
Pete Crow-Armstrong wrapped up the NL MVP award weeks ago. Now, in the final week of the regular season, the Cubs centerfielder is looking to put the finishing touches on one of the greatest all-around campaigns in baseball history.
Triple threat: PCA might not pitch like his onetime MVP competition Shohei Ohtani, but he does wield the best glove in the league in addition to his otherworldly combination of power and speed.
- At the plate he's batting .280 with an NL-best .949 OPS on the strength of 45 home runs. Yes, the speedy centerfielder is now tied with Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead. He also leads the majors in runs (118) and extra-base hits (83), and ranks third in RBI (107).
- In the field he leads all players in outs above average (26) and fielding run value (27). His 50% success rate (8 of 16) on 5-star catches (those with a Statcast probability of 0-25%) is also by far the best in the majors.
Put another way: He's having the best offensive season of anyone outside of Yordan Alvarez, but while the Astros slugger spends almost all of his time at designated hitter, PCA has also been the single best fielder in baseball at any position.
Big picture: Add it all up, and Crow-Armstrong has amassed 10.4 wins above replacement at FanGraphs, making him just the seventh position player this century to post a 10-fWAR season. But as impressive as that is in a vacuum, it's in the comparison to his peers where it transcends to historic territory.
- Perhaps you've heard of the other three men to accomplish that feat: Babe Ruth (3x), Rogers Hornsby (2x) and Mickey Mantle. Adjusted for era, PCA's season has to be considered one of the greatest ever. And to think, we almost didn't get it.
Midseason change: It's easy to forget now, but PCA had a terrible spring, batting .224 with 6 HR and a .676 OPS in 55 games from Opening Day through May 26. As the poor results kept coming and he drifted further away from the player who'd shown flashes of superstardom a year earlier, he and Chicago's coaching staff decided to drastically alter his stance.
- The changes, as laid out by WSJ's Jared Diamond ($), were three-fold: He stands closer to the plate and deeper in the box, his legs are a foot closer together, and he holds his hands at his chest with the bat pointing up rather than at shoulder-level with the bat parallel to the ground.
- Safe to say it worked. In 101 games since the changes began taking hold, he's hitting .307 with 39 home runs and a 1.079 OPS.
The last word: "You're grateful to see things like this," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said last week after PCA's seventh multi-homer game of the season. "And you're grateful that the fans get to see a season like this, because they're going to talk about it. They're going to tell their kids about it. They're going to tell their grandkids about seasons like this."
🌍 The world in photos
🇺🇸 Los Angeles, California
The Rams destroyed the Giants in their home opener, 28-6, behind huge games from Matthew Stafford (22/31, 327 yards, 4 TD) and Davante Adams (8 catches, 195 yards, 2 TD). New York, meanwhile, joined the injured QB club* as Jaxson Dart was knocked out in the first quarter with what appears to be a sprained MCL.
Climbing the leaderboard: With 427 career passing touchdowns, Stafford passed Philip Rivers (425) for sixth-most in NFL history. He'll need to play at least another couple seasons to catch Brett Favre (508) in fifth, and may have a little more trouble catching Aaron Rodgers (528), Peyton Manning (539), Drew Brees (571) and Tom Brady (649).
🇫🇷 Clairefontaine-en-Yvelines, France
Zinedine Zidane oversaw his first training session on Monday since becoming France's new head coach, with his first test coming in Friday's Nations League match against Turkey. The international break, which at 16 days is the longest ever, runs through Oct. 6.
Why so long? This is the first such break under FIFA's new calendar, which has been reconfigured to limit travel and minimize disruptions to domestic club schedules. Instead of three short breaks in the fall and one in the spring, there are now two in the fall and one in the spring.
🇨🇦 Montreal, Canada
Belgium's Remco Evenepoel dominated the field on Sunday for his record-tying fourth time trial world title, becoming the first cyclist to win the event four years in a row. That continues an excellent year that also saw the two-time Olympic champion finish second to Tadej Pogačar in the Tour de France.
The secret to his success: At 5-foot-7, Evenepoel is smaller than most elite time trialists, but what he lacks in mass he makes up for with his uniquely compact riding position. "He can almost put his head into his trunk and into his arms, and he's still able to look forward," says Evenepoel's physio. "That's why they call him 'the bullet.'"
*QB injury updates: Chicago's Caleb Williams (hamstring) "will likely miss some time" but avoided a serious injury and Washington's Jayden Daniels (dislocated elbow) will meet with specialists this week. On the flip side, Minnesota's Kyler Murray (concussion) and Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr. (ACL surgery recovery) will both start in Week 3.
👟 Mbappé moves On
In June, Kylian Mbappé featured centrally in Nike's "Rip the Script" World Cup short film, shortly before tearing through defenses in Nike boots throughout the tournament. Just three months later, his long-time relationship with the Swoosh has ended. Mbappé is moving On… or to On, in this case.
Catch up: Swiss sportswear brand On announced on Friday that it's entering football alongside the French superstar. Mbappé will be a global ambassador for the brand, working closely with product teams in developing football footwear and apparel.
What it means: This is perhaps the most ambitious extension of On's brand yet, as it tries to establish itself at the highest ranks of the world's most popular sport. However, the company has a track record in precisely this sort of endeavor, executed with a very similar playbook.
History doesn't repeat itself, but it rhymes: The last time On shocked the sports world with a signing of this magnitude, the brand was a lesser-known commodity. Its prize in 2019? Swiss tennis legend Roger Federer, who invested in the company and supported its efforts to build a tennis business. On's efforts in tennis, anchored by Federer and aided by stars like Iga Świątek and Ben Shelton, demonstrate its ability to grow from a nonexistent presence to a major player at a sport's elite levels. With Mbappé in tow, it will try to make the same leap in football.
This is an excerpt from Monday's edition of Yahoo Sports Biz, our new sports business newsletter. Sign up here to get on the list.
🏀 NBA preseason power rankings
With the NBA season tipping off in less than a month (Oct. 20), Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor has ranked every team's chances of winning the 2027 NBA Championship, while also surveying what's changed during the offseason, what's exciting and what's concerning for each team.
⚽️ Barcelona are unstoppable
Barcelona have opened their 2026-27 campaign in another stratosphere, laying waste to the competition with a goal-scoring frenzy the likes of which haven't been seen in nearly a century.
36 goals for, 8 against: Barça are undefeated in eight matches entering the international break, scoring 31 goals across their first seven La Liga fixtures (second-most in league history behind Sevilla in 1940), and 36 if you include their Champions League opener (their most through eight matches since 1935).
- Barcelona 5, Elche 0
- Barcelona 2, Athletic Club 0
- Barcelona 5, Rayo Vallecano 2
- Barcelona 5, Valenica 0
- Barcelona 5, Feyenoord Rotterdam 1
- Barcelona 4, Levante 2
- Barcelona 7, Racing Santander 2
- Barcelona 3, Sevilla 1
Dynamic duo: At the center of the carnage are Brazilian striker Raphinha and Spanish winger Lamine Yamal, who've combined for 22 goals and nine assists on the young season. Raphinha's 12 domestic goals lead La Liga by a wide margin, while his three assists are tied for second; Lamine's seven goals are tied for second, and his four assists are tied for first.
Go deeper: This is the best Barcelona have looked under Hansi Flick (The Athletic)

The AL East rivals begin their four-game series with a split doubleheader (1:05pm ET, ESPN+; 7:05pm, TBS), and though the division hasn't been decided yet, the race is all but over. Best of the rest: The wild-card bound Red Sox (84-72) host the Guardians (81-75), who hold a one-game lead in the AL Central (6:45pm); the White Sox (80-76), currently in the third wild card and chasing Cleveland for the division, visit the Royals (7:40pm); the Rangers (78-78) host the Mets (8:05pm) with a one-game lead in the AL West over the Astros (77-79), who visit the Mariners in the nightcap (9:40pm).

The Women's Professional Baseball League will crown its inaugural champion tonight (7pm, ESPN+) when the San Francisco Firebells — who've fought back from an 0-2 deficit — take on the Los Angeles Queens in a decisive Game 5.
Players to watch: This series features arguably the two biggest names in women's baseball. The Firebells are led by No. 1 pick Kelsie Whitmore, a two-way player who hit a league-leading 11 HR this season while also starting six games on the mound; the Queens boast Mo'ne Davis, the trailblazing star of the 2014 Little League World Series.

item.title: [The Ringer] Baseball’s Best Pitchers Aren’t Worth What They Used to Be (But Its Best Batters Are)
item.description: On Sunday, as MLB’s regular season reached its one-week warning, the two most spectacular players of 2026 strutted their stuff. In Cincinnati, Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong singled, doubled, and hit his 45th home run in a 9-1 trouncing of the Reds. (He also stole his 38th base, putting him on the precipice of joining the 40-40 club.)
